title: Solana DEX Velocity halts trading over bug just months after relaunch
summary: Velocity relaunched in September as a rebuilt version of Drift Protocol, which was attacked by North Korean hackers in April.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 25, 2026

Velocity relaunched in September as a rebuilt version of Drift Protocol, which was attacked by North Korean hackers in April.

Solana-based decentralized exchange Velocity said Wednesday it has suspended all transactions while its team works to fix a bug.

“User deposits are safe,” Velocity said in a post on X, and that the protocol would remain paused until it was safe to resume.

Velocity is the rebuilt, forked version of Drift Protocol, which was hacked in April. Velocity relaunched under the new name in September.

Unlike Drift Protocol, Velocity DEX focuses exclusively on perpetual futures trading, removing standalone spot trading. Data from DefiLlama shows its perp volume saw a significant spike in November, with the biggest spike in volume on Nov. 18 and 19.

Velocity said it will share more about the bug on social media.

Drift reported about $295 million in losses from an April 1 hack, which has been blamed on UNC6862, a North Korean threat group.

Related: Drift exploiter sends $61M ETH to Tornado Cash, holds $194M

title: Over 2,200 Institutions Held $29.8B in Bitcoin ETFs, Advisers Led
summary: Bloomberg Intelligence counted 2,223 filers with spot bitcoin ETF holdings worth $29.8 billion at the end of the third quarter. Investment advisers made up about 84% of the filers and accounted for $13.4 billion in exposure. Investment Advisers Made Up 84% of Bitcoin ETF Filers James Seyffart, senio...
content:
Bloomberg Intelligence counted 2,223 filers with spot bitcoin ETF holdings worth $29.8 billion at the end of the third quarter. Investment advisers made up about 84% of the filers and accounted for $13.4 billion in exposure.

Key Takeaways

  • Bloomberg identified 2,223 filers with $29.8 billion in bitcoin ETFs.
  • Investment advisers accounted for 1,863 filers and $13.4 billion.
  • Wells Fargo led parent companies with $2.55 billion in exposure.

Investment Advisers Made Up 84% of Bitcoin ETF Filers

James Seyffart, senior ETF analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, shared on Nov. 24 that his breakdown of bitcoin ETF ownership identified 2,223 Form 13F filers with spot bitcoin ETF holdings as of Sept. 30. Their $29.8 billion in reported positions represented exposure equivalent to 356,072 bitcoin.

He wrote on X:

“The known ownership is dominated by investment advisors though.”

The 1,863 investment advisers accounted for about 45% of the reported dollar exposure. Brokerages ranked second by value, with 49 filers accounting for nearly $5 billion. Another 141 hedge fund managers had $4.86 billion in exposure, while 86 banks had $2.42 billion.

Galaxy Counted 2,166 Managers in Spot Bitcoin Funds

Galaxy Research’s Q3 bitcoin ETF ownership analysis counted 2,166 managers using filings through Nov. 17, up 191 from June 30. Half held positions equivalent to less than 10.4 bitcoin, or about $870,000 at quarter-end prices. Its tally covered 13 spot bitcoin funds, including one that trades over the counter.

The firm’s analysis put quarter-end institutional ETF exposure at roughly the same dollar total as Bloomberg’s. Galaxy estimated that managers added the equivalent of 49,229 bitcoin during the quarter, their biggest quarterly increase since the second quarter of 2025.

Wells Fargo Led When Affiliates Were Combined

Wells Fargo & Co. (NYSE: WFC) ranked first in Bloomberg’s parent-company tally at $2.55 billion. Jane Street Group LLC placed second at $1.91 billion. Jane Street led the individual-entity rankings, followed by Wells Fargo Clearing Services LLC at $1.63 billion.

Most of Wells Fargo’s total came from its $2.35 billion Blackrock position. Five affiliated managers disclosed a combined 49.58 million Ishares Bitcoin Trust ETF shares, up from 24.40 million at the end of June. Two brokerage affiliates accounted for about 85% of the September share count.

What the Filings Capture

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) generally requires quarterly disclosures from institutional managers with discretion over at least $100 million in securities covered by Form 13F. The filings can include positions held for clients or the manager’s own account. Managers report only long positions and do not subtract short positions in the same security.

Quarter-end holdings describe positions on a specific date. Fund flows track subscriptions and redemptions, one factor in liquidity across bitcoin markets. An ETF can register net redemptions while some investors hold their positions, and daily flow totals do not identify which Form 13F filers traded.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded net redemptions across funds of $4.71 billion in November through Nov. 23. The funds posted $569.74 million in net withdrawals that day, extending their outflow streak to five trading sessions. Blackrock’s fund accounted for about $1.6 billion in withdrawals over three sessions.

title: Trump willing to pardon Jensen Huang, says it won’t be necessary
summary: The president’s remarks come days before Jensen Huang is due to face congressional questioning over national security concerns and US chip export controls.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 25, 2026

The president’s remarks come days before Jensen Huang is due to face congressional questioning over national security concerns and US chip export controls.

US President Donald Trump has left the door open to pardoning Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang, though he said he doesn’t think it’ll be necessary.

Trump made the comments during an interview with the New York Post just a day after Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO amid scrutiny over his affair with a suspected Chinese spy and whether he allowed the company’s chips to fall into China’s hands.

Asked about a pardon for any potential crimes, Trump told The Post: “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”

Trump had earlier claimed credit for pushing Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back — a move which saw Nvidia’s stock surge on Monday.

Huang is scheduled to testify before lawmakers in a closed-door, transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Intelligence Committee and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party on Dec. 1.

On Dec. 3, Huang is set to be the sole witness in a hearing by the Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs about US export controls.

title: Samson Mow Offers to Join Nvidia’s Board to Push Bitcoin Strategy
summary: JAN3 CEO Samson Mow offered to join Nvidia’s board and urged the chipmaker to buy bitcoin, citing about $29 billion in cash holdings. His offer followed Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO and a board director. Mow Offers to Join Nvidia’s Board Samson Mow, chief executive officer of bitcoin...
content:
JAN3 CEO Samson Mow offered to join Nvidia’s board and urged the chipmaker to buy bitcoin, citing about $29 billion in cash holdings. His offer followed Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO and a board director.

Key Takeaways

  • Samson Mow offered to join Nvidia’s board to push a bitcoin strategy.
  • Nvidia held $29.09 billion in cash and cash equivalents on Oct. 25.
  • A unanimous board vote restored Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO.

Mow Offers to Join Nvidia’s Board

Samson Mow, chief executive officer of bitcoin technology company JAN3, offered to join Nvidia’s board on Nov. 23. He tied his offer to a bitcoin strategy for Nvidia (Nasdaq: NVDA) that he would support under CEO Jensen Huang, whose return the chipmaker announced earlier that day.

He wrote on X:

“I am willing to join the new Nvidia board and support Jensen Huang to aggressively pursue a Bitcoin strategy for $NVDA.”

The offer followed an earlier message in which Mow told Huang to “clean house on the board.” The bitcoin technology company he leads focuses on expanding access to bitcoin and financial freedom worldwide.

In another X post, Mow wrote:

“NVIDIA should not be holding $29B in melting fiat currency. It’s time to buy bitcoin.”

Nvidia Held $29.09 Billion in Cash and Equivalents

The chipmaker’s quarterly balance sheet showed $29.09 billion in cash and cash equivalents as of Oct. 25, up from $10.61 billion on Jan. 25. Nvidia listed another $24.42 billion in marketable debt securities and $44.22 billion in marketable equity securities.

The same financial disclosure showed that Nvidia spent $22.12 billion on common stock repurchases and paid $6.03 billion in dividends during the quarter. Mow cited the cash balance when urging Nvidia to buy bitcoin.

Nvidia’s Board Reinstated Huang as CEO

A unanimous Nvidia board vote reinstated Huang as president, CEO, and director. Harvey C. Jones remained board chair, and Colette Kress, who had served as interim CEO, continued as chief financial officer. Nvidia said its independent investigation into reports that a foreign intelligence effort targeted Huang would continue.

Responses to Huang’s return to Nvidia ranged from support to calls for scrutiny. Elon Musk, President Donald Trump, and Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) welcomed the decision, while Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chuck Schumer raised questions about export controls and government involvement.

Mow Tags Strive CEO Matt Cole

Mow tagged Strive CEO Matt Cole in another reply and asked him to make it happen. Cole had disclosed Strive’s $2.2 million bitcoin purchase on Nov. 9. The purchase of 29 bitcoin raised the holdings of Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) to 43,153 BTC.

Companies with a corporate bitcoin treasury can hold the asset alongside cash or other reserves. The size of the allocation determines how much of the balance sheet is exposed to swings in bitcoin’s price.

Strategy (Nasdaq: MSTR) disclosed a 457-bitcoin purchase for $29.6 million on Nov. 23, bringing its holdings to 851,305 BTC alongside $4.8 billion in U.S. dollar assets.

Key Features of Hyperliquid Crypto Exchange

On-Chain Order Book

Most decentralized exchanges use off-chain order books or automated market makers due to the high throughput required by on-chain order books. However, the platform runs its order book on-chain, providing transparency, security, and speed-optimized transactions through its custom consensus mechanism, HyperBFT, which can confirm up to 200,000 transactions per second using Byzantine Fault Tolerance.

Gas-Free Transactions

Since Hyperliquid operates on its own Layer 1 chain, it controls the entire infrastructure and does not require users to pay gas fees for transactions, unlike Ethereum or other public blockchains. Instead, the platform covers the underlying transaction costs internally and charges users only minimal fees.

High Leverage Trading

Hyperliquid offers up to 40x leverage on perpetual futures contracts, allowing traders to amplify their positions beyond what their actual trading capital can carry. Due to the high risk associated with leverage trading, this feature is particularly tailored to experienced traders who are familiar with the strategy and want to increase their profit potential from rapid market movements.

Liquidity Vaults

Liquidity vaults on Hyperliquid are created by individuals or entities who want to share their trading strategies with others. Users can deposit funds into these vaults and earn a share of the profits or losses based on the vault leader’s trading performance. Aside from user-owned vaults, the Hyperliquid platform features protocol vaults, such as the Hyperliquidity Provider (HLP) Vault, which acts as a market maker and liquidation mechanism, earning a portion of the trading fees.

Cross-Chain Compatibility

Previously, users had to bridge into Arbitrum before accessing Hyperliquid. This integration eliminates the previous process that required traders to bridge funds through Arbitrum before accessing Hyperliquid.

Pro-level Trading Tools

Another standout feature of Hyperliquid is the advanced trading tools available to traders, which are similar to those used by professional traders on traditional exchanges. This includes features such as the on-chain order book, real-time charts, customizable order types (including limit, market, and stop orders), in-depth market data, and responsive user interfaces, catering to both retail and institutional traders.

What Are the Pros and Cons of Hyperliquid?

The pros of Hyperliquid are listed below:

  • Advanced Trading Features: Hyperliquid offers a wide range of trading options, including spot trading, perpetual trading, pre-launch futures contracts, margin trading, and up to 40x leverage. Additionally, it supports multiple order types, including market, limit, stop market, stop limit, scale, and TWAP orders, providing traders with advanced tools to execute various strategies.

title: XRP ETF Brings Bitwise $667M in Inflows and $3.5B in First-Year Trades
summary: Bitwise’s XRP ETF recorded over $667 million in net inflows and more than $3.5 billion in trading volume during its first year. The fund also managed approximately $377 million in assets. Bitwise XRP ETF Completes Its First Year Bitwise Asset Management summarized the first year of its XRP exchange-...
content:
Bitwise’s XRP ETF recorded over $667 million in net inflows and more than $3.5 billion in trading volume during its first year. The fund also managed approximately $377 million in assets.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitwise’s XRP ETF attracted $667M in first-year net inflows.
  • Trading volume surpassed $3.5B, averaging about $14M daily.
  • Assets stood near $377M after the fund’s first year.

Bitwise XRP ETF Completes Its First Year

Bitwise Asset Management summarized the first year of its XRP exchange-traded fund (ETF) on Nov. 24 in an X post, reporting more than $376 million in assets under management. The firm’s first-year XRP ETF figures included over $667 million in net inflows and more than $3.5 billion in total traded volume.

The asset manager wrote:

“XRP has been part of crypto’s story for more than a decade, through every cycle, and it’s still helping shape what comes next.”

The ETF began trading on NYSE Arca under the ticker XRP on Nov. 20, 2025, following its formal launch announcement one day earlier. Bitwise’s XRP ETF launch announcement listed a 0.34% management fee and confirmed that the fund would hold spot XRP.

Its cumulative trading volume averaged approximately $14 million per trading day during the period, according to Bitwise. That figure measures the value of shares exchanged in the market, while net inflows represent capital entering the fund after subtracting redemptions.

Why Inflows Exceed Current Assets

Assets under management measure the fund’s current net value rather than the total capital it has attracted. The figure changes with XRP’s market price, share creations and redemptions, and expenses.

The fund’s latest quarterly SEC filing listed $614.85 million in net assets as of Sept. 30. It held approximately 413.14 million XRP valued at $615 million, with 36.99 million shares outstanding and a net asset value of $16.62 per share.

Bitwise’s XRP ETF had crossed $500 million in net assets by late August, nine months after its debut. At that point, the fund held nearly 364.8 million XRP, compared with about 286.8 million at the end of the second quarter.

The first-year figures place current assets substantially below cumulative net inflows. Assets and cumulative inflows measure different factors, with the former moving alongside the market value of XRP held by the fund.

Bitwise’s fund page showed 401.19 million XRP in the trust and $376.84 million in net assets on Nov. 23. Token holdings were down about 3% from Sept. 30, while net assets had fallen roughly 39%, putting the implied value of each XRP held near $0.94, compared with about $1.49 at the end of September.

XRP Funds Draw Institutional Positions

Bitwise remained one of the largest U.S. products offering spot XRP exposure. By late September, seven U.S. XRP funds held nearly 1.18 billion XRP, with Bitwise leading the group at approximately 413.1 million tokens.

Quarterly securities filings later showed banks and trading firms holding shares in the fund. Intesa Sanpaolo disclosed a Bitwise position valued at $6.70 million, while Jane Street reported approximately $12.20 million and several other institutions held smaller stakes.

Those filings reflected positions as of Sept. 30 and do not establish whether the institutions retained the shares afterward. The disclosures can include securities managed for clients as well as holdings maintained for a firm’s own account.

Investors in the Bitwise XRP ETF own exchange-listed shares rather than XRP they can transfer or use on the XRP Ledger. This distinction between exchange-traded exposure and direct crypto ownership leaves custody of the underlying tokens with the fund’s appointed custodian.

title: CleanSpark weighs selling more Bitcoin than it mines to de-risk books
summary: The Bitcoin miner sold 2,102 BTC while it produced just 1,708 BTC in the September quarter.
content:
Bitcoin miner CleanSpark is considering selling more Bitcoin than it mines each quarter to reduce its treasury risk, according to chief financial officer Gary Vecchiarelli, potentially further drawing down its holdings, last valued at $806 million.

CleanSpark held 13,530 Bitcoin at the end of September after mining 1,708 Bitcoin and selling 2,102 Bitcoin during the quarter, according to Cointelegraph’s tally of the company’s monthly operating updates. It marks the first time since at least 2024 that the company ended the quarter with less Bitcoin than it began with.

During a Q4 earnings call on Tuesday, Vecchiarelli said CleanSpark already aims to sell virtually all of the Bitcoin it mines to cover day-to-day operating costs, and told an analyst that selling slightly more than it produces in a quarter was one way to reduce treasury risk.

“We see the selling of a small amount of Bitcoin in excess of the quarterly production to be one way of de-risking,” said Vecchiarelli.

“But again, we are going to be sensitive and very reactionary to markets, and we are going to use that capital to make sure that we prevent dilution or bringing additional debt just to grow the company,” he said.

The remarks came as CleanSpark recorded a $987 million net loss for the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, compared with a net income of $364 million a year earlier. The company attributed two-thirds of the swing to noncash adjustments in the value of its Bitcoin holdings, as Bitcoin’s price fell from about $114,100 to $83,600 over the fiscal year.

Related: Trump-linked American Bitcoin secures $150M credit line from FalconX

CleanSpark also said it sold an undisclosed amount of Bitcoin since September to raise cash for expected acquisitions, as Vecchiarelli said it continues to view its Bitcoin holdings as “a liquid source of non-dilutive capital.”

CleanSpark trims mining fleet as AI buildout advances

CleanSpark also cut about 25,000 machines from its Bitcoin mining fleet in the September quarter, bringing the number in operation to about 200,000.

Vecchiarelli said the reduction improved energy efficiency to 14.8 joules per terahash from 15.8 in the previous quarter, which he said should help CleanSpark stay profitable if mining conditions deteriorate ahead of the 2028 Bitcoin halving.

“Going forward, in terms of hash rate, that will probably fluctuate, but we will continue to mine so as long as it’s profitable.”

In Sandersville, Georgia, CleanSpark said its first AI data hall remains on track for the fourth quarter of 2027. CleanSpark said it expects to start unplugging miners at the site in late 2027 as the data center comes online, then decide whether to relocate or sell them.

CleanSpark shares dropped 7.5% on Tuesday ahead of the earnings release to $5.12 and are down 2.25% in after-hours trading.

The company recorded $576.5 million in total revenue in the full year, down 25% from the previous fiscal year. Adjusted EBITDA came in at a loss of $304.2 million for the year.

title: 21shares Dissects Bitcoin’s Selling Spiral as the Market Eyes $53K
summary: Crypto asset manager 21shares warns that bitcoin’s recovery attempts could remain short-lived as shrinking stablecoin liquidity, institutional withdrawals and forced liquidations prolong the bear market. Researchers identify $53,250 as a significant downside level, while prediction market traders an...
content:
Crypto asset manager 21shares warns that bitcoin’s recovery attempts could remain short-lived as shrinking stablecoin liquidity, institutional withdrawals and forced liquidations prolong the bear market. Researchers identify $53,250 as a significant downside level, while prediction market traders anticipate similar valuations.

Key Takeaways

  • 21shares attributes bitcoin’s steepest losses to weakening demand and forced selling rather than the Binance hack itself.
  • November bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) withdrawals have reached a record $4.71 billion as Monday’s Nvidia-driven rally evaporated.
  • Kalshi traders assign a 59% probability to bitcoin falling below $55,000 before 2027.

21shares Identifies Three Forces Behind Bitcoin’s Deepening Bear Market

The Binance hack lit the match, but evaporating demand and excessive leverage supplied the fuel. In a research report published Tuesday, Nov. 24, crypto asset manager 21shares dissected the mechanics behind bitcoin’s latest downturn, identifying three distinct phases of market deterioration.

The market assessment, authored by Eliezer Ndinga with additional analysis from Karim Abdelmawla, Maximiliaan Michelsen and Matthew Mena, suggests the cryptocurrency economy remains vulnerable to prolonged defensive positioning.

Bitcoin initially lost 5.1% in the two days following the Binance breach before recovering to $80,488 by Nov. 4. Even by Nov. 9, the leading cryptocurrency remained just 7% below its pre-hack valuation. The analysis notes that the heavier damage followed as capital began draining from the market. Between Nov. 4 and 11, bitcoin fell 8.3% to $73,806 as stablecoin liquidity and institutional demand deteriorated.

Stablecoin supply contracted by $10.7 billion following the breach, marking the largest 18-day dollar-denominated reduction since Terra’s 2022 collapse. Exchange-held stablecoin balances declined 15%, while U.S. spot bitcoin and ethereum exchange-traded funds (ETFs) collectively lost $3.9 billion between Oct. 30 and Nov. 13.

Forced selling subsequently accelerated the decline. Bitcoin dropped another 13.5% between Nov. 11 and 14, with $1.6 billion in leveraged bitcoin longs liquidated over three days. Across cryptocurrency markets, weekly liquidations reached $5.8 billion through Nov. 15, with longs accounting for 81%.

Bitcoin’s Failed Nvidia Rally Exposes Fragile Demand

Monday’s trading session offered a timely illustration of the conditions described by the 21shares researchers. Bitcoin climbed to approximately $65,200 after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, triggering a broad recovery across financial markets.

While technology stocks largely retained their gains, bitcoin surrendered its advance, returning back under the $60,000 region Tuesday afternoon. November’s institutional withdrawals have also reached unprecedented levels.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $569.7 million in withdrawals Monday, with Blackrock’s IBIT accounting for approximately $509 million. November’s cumulative outflows reached a record $4.71 billion.

Glassnode data indicates bitcoin investors are realizing their heaviest losses since the FTX collapse. “Bitcoin losses are the heaviest since FTX,” Glassnode analysts wrote on Tuesday. “Set against the money that flowed into Bitcoin over the past year, they have almost doubled in a week. Spikes like this often came close to past lows, but some came early.”

Meanwhile, Cryptoquant figures show long-term holders selling into the recovery at losses of approximately 33%. “Long-term holders sold at a 33% loss into bitcoin’s rebound, a level last seen at the June bottom,” Cryptoquant shared on X.

Community sentiment remains deeply fractured, with some cryptocurrency enthusiasts anticipating further capitulation toward $40,000 and others interpreting distressed selling as evidence that the prolonged bear market may be approaching exhaustion.

Bitcoin’s $53,250 Realized Price Emerges as Key Level

Having already breached $60,000, bitcoin faces another significant threshold identified by 21shares: its realized price of approximately $53,250. The metric measures bitcoin’s aggregate cost basis using the valuation at which coins last moved onchain.

Applying historical bear market discounts produces illustrative downside scenarios of $40,400 and $37,200. The researchers consider such declines relatively unlikely for now, citing institutional participation absent from earlier cycles.

Interestingly, the assessment follows 21shares’ Nov. 19 digital asset outlook, which anticipated a new bitcoin all-time high in 2027. As Bitcoin.com News previously reported, historical comparisons in that publication illustrated valuations between $129,000 and $146,000 by mid-2027.

The latest analysis does not explicitly abandon that longer-term outlook, instead emphasizing the immediate obstacles standing between bitcoin and a sustainable recovery.

Prediction Market Traders Anticipate a $53K Floor

Kalshi’s annual bitcoin minimum-price market, which has accumulated $9.91 million in trading volume, currently indicates a projected floor of $53,000, closely aligning with the realized price highlighted by 21shares. Participants assign a 59% probability to bitcoin falling below $55,000 before 2027, a 32% probability to breaching $50,000 and a 16% chance of slipping beneath $45,000.

Kalshi’s November-specific market assigns a 27% probability to sub-$55,000 bitcoin before December, with nearly $2 million in trading volume. On Polymarket, traders assessing bitcoin’s price at noon Eastern time on Dec. 1 favor two adjacent brackets: $58,000 to $60,000 and $60,000 to $62,000, each carrying a 19% implied probability. However, the market’s modest $1,456 trading volume warrants caution when interpreting those readings.

Bitcoin Veterans Debate What Could Ignite the Next Bull Market

The deteriorating market has also reignited debate over bitcoin’s long-term investment thesis. Trinary AI co-founder and CEO Vinny Lingham took to X, questioning what catalysts remain after years of monetary expansion, institutional adoption, elevated inflation and declining bitcoin issuance. Lingham pointed out that bitcoin is trading below its valuation five years ago despite many of the bullish narratives from 2021 having materialized. “What’s the catalyst for the bull case in light of this?” he asked.

The question elicited divergent responses from industry veterans. Former Bitinstant CEO Charlie Shrem challenged the tendency to retrospectively assign catalysts to market cycles, stating, “We don’t know why those bull markets happened, we lived through them and then assigned reasons postmortem.” Stacks co-founder Muneeb Ali identified native bitcoin yield, credible quantum-resistant upgrades, artificial intelligence (AI) safeguards and the 2028 halving as potential catalysts.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg commodity strategist Mike McGlone, who has floated a $10,000 bitcoin price scenario, offered a decidedly more bearish perspective: “Don’t fight the Fed, especially with highly volatile and correlated to beta assets within a space of unlimited supply.”

For 21shares, expanding stablecoin liquidity and sustained ETF inflows remain essential ingredients for a meaningful reversal. Monday’s fleeting recovery demonstrated that favorable headlines can temporarily interrupt a bear market, but without fresh capital entering the cryptocurrency economy, even the most encouraging catalysts may accomplish little beyond postponing the next round of selling.

title: Ethereum Foundation Warns AI Threats Outpace Quantum, Doubles Security Team
summary: The Ethereum Foundation has doubled the size of its protocol security team after warning that artificial intelligence poses a more immediate threat to the blockchain than quantum computing. Ethereum Foundation Warns AI Is Speeding Up Software Attacks Ethereum is preparing to overhaul the cryptograph...
content:
The Ethereum Foundation has doubled the size of its protocol security team after warning that artificial intelligence poses a more immediate threat to the blockchain than quantum computing.

Key Takeaways

  • Ethereum doubled its security team as AI speeds vulnerability discovery.
  • Hash-based cryptography could replace key Ethereum security systems by 2028.
  • The challenge is upgrading security without hurting network reliability.

Ethereum Foundation Warns AI Is Speeding Up Software Attacks

Ethereum is preparing to overhaul the cryptography protecting its network as rapid advances in artificial intelligence force developers to reconsider long-standing security assumptions.

In a Nov. 23 blog post, Ethereum Foundation researcher Kev Wedderburn warned that AI models are discovering vulnerabilities in production software faster than human developers can review them.

The foundation has spent years researching quantum computing threats. However, AI’s growing ability to identify software flaws and improve mathematical algorithms has accelerated its security plans.

“This upgrade is harder than the Merge, and we have less time,” Wedderburn wrote, referring to Ethereum’s transition to proof-of-stake in September 2022.

Ethereum Plans Major Cryptographic Overhaul

The proposed changes would fundamentally alter how Ethereum validates transactions, secures user accounts, and processes blockchain data.

Validators would adopt hash-based signatures, replacing their reliance on elliptic-curve cryptography. Wallets would support similar protections, while data blobs used by Layer 2 scaling networks would shift to hash-based commitments.

These changes would affect wallet providers, staking pools, smart contracts, and other infrastructure across the crypto ecosystem.

To address implementation risks, the Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team and prioritized formal verification, a process used to mathematically check software correctness.

The transition could force developers to postpone features that have been under development for years.

Ethereum Targets 2028 as AI Accelerates Security Concerns

Ethereum researcher Justin Drake proposed December 2028 as a target for the security transition during Devcon in Mumbai.

The foundation maintains an internal deadline of 2029, with a timeline review scheduled for January 2027. Early technical specifications and test networks are already under development.

The foundation also cited a recent AI-assisted claim to have solved the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis. The mathematical breakthrough remains subject to expert scrutiny, and the foundation acknowledged that AI has not demonstrated an ability to break Ethereum’s existing cryptography.

For Ethereum’s developers and millions of crypto users, the stakes extend beyond theoretical security risks. The challenge now is implementing sweeping protections without undermining the network’s reliability or accessibility.

title: Hackers breach CIA intelligence network in latest US cyberattack
summary: The reported breach follows cyber incidents involving the FBI, Department of Homeland Security and Department of Agriculture.
content:
The US Central Intelligence Agency and at least one other intelligence agency have been hit with a cybersecurity breach that exposed unclassified information, according to The New York Times.

Citing US officials and people familiar with the matter, the Times reported that hackers breached a network used by the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence that analyzes publicly available information to gather intelligence insights.

It is also believed that other government agencies were exposed in the breach, according to two of the people.

An official with the Office of the Director of National Intelligence said there have been no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems. Cointelegraph reached out to the CIA for comment.

The breach adds to a spate of reported cyber incidents at US federal agencies in recent weeks.

The Verge on Tuesday reported the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) is also investigating a “cybersecurity incident” that “resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.” It is not clear if it is related to the recent CIA breach.

Other breaches include the US Department of Agriculture, a leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel records and a hack of the FBI’s national crime database.

Speaking to ABC News about the FBI attack on Sunday, US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said cyberattacks have been increasing, and digital infrastructure needs to be upgraded.

“In 2020, there were roughly 750,000 cyber incidents reported to the FBI. That’s now up to over a million cyber incidents,” said Clayton.

“And what we’re seeing, though, here, and I want the American people to know this, is we have a step change in technology that we’re facing with superintelligence and computing power that is expanding exponentially and we have a dated digital infrastructure.”

Clayton declined to discuss the specifics of the FBI incident but said that cyber incidents were not a new phenomenon.

“Cyber probing, cyber incidents, they have been part of the American economy, part of the American life for a long time.”

title: CFTC Opens Door to Bitcoin, Ether and Stablecoins as Operating Reserves
summary: CFTC staff issued an advisory allowing exchanges and clearinghouses to count bitcoin, ether, and payment stablecoins toward 12-month operating reserve requirements. Solvency Buffer vs. Liquidity Carve-Out Staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) issued an advisory on Nov. 23 clarifyi...
content:
CFTC staff issued an advisory allowing exchanges and clearinghouses to count bitcoin, ether, and payment stablecoins toward 12-month operating reserve requirements.

Key Takeaways

  • CFTC staff clarified that bitcoin, ether, and payment stablecoins can count toward 12-month operating reserves.
  • Crypto assets remain excluded from cash liquidity buffers because GAAP does not classify them as cash equivalents.
  • Industry observers note the 20% and 2% haircuts give firms balance-sheet flexibility while pricing in market risk.

Solvency Buffer vs. Liquidity Carve-Out

Staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) issued an advisory on Nov. 23 clarifying that regulated derivatives venues and clearinghouses may count bitcoin (BTC), ether (ETH), and payment stablecoins toward their 12-month operating-cost financial resource requirements, subject to valuation haircuts.

The joint advisory from the Division of Market Oversight and the Division of Clearing and Risk addresses how swap execution facilities (SEFs), designated contract markets (DCMs), and derivatives clearing organizations (DCOs) satisfy capital obligations under CFTC regulations 37.1301, 38.1101(a), and 39.11(a)(2). Under those rules, registered entities must maintain sufficient financial resources to cover at least 12 months of rolling operating expenses.

While staff confirmed that qualifying digital assets can help satisfy that one-year solvency cushion, the guidance drew a strict boundary around immediate cash liquidity. Because Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) do not classify cryptocurrencies or stablecoins as “cash” or “highly liquid securities,” firms cannot use digital assets to meet the separate liquidity requirement, typically three months of operating costs for SEFs and six months for DCMs and DCOs.

Soham Jethani, managing partner at Septten Advisors, said the distinction between holding balance-sheet assets and holding cash ready to pay immediate bills is critical for market infrastructure operators.

“That is sensible: a business exposed to crypto markets could see its income and the value of its reserves fall overnight if they have the wrong portfolio,” Jethani noted, adding that the framework gives venues greater flexibility to utilize invested assets that previously received no regulatory recognition.

Valuation Haircuts and Market Depth

To account for price volatility and market risk, the staff guidance subjects eligible holdings to minimum valuation discounts, at least 20% for bitcoin and ether and 2% for payment stablecoins, while assigning a 100% haircut to non-readily marketable tokens. Under the 20% threshold, $1 million in bitcoin counts for no more than $800,000 toward operating reserves.

Jethani pointed out that focusing on bitcoin and ether reflects both regulatory precedent—drawing on existing staff treatment of futures brokers’ proprietary crypto holdings—and market liquidity.

“Bitcoin and ether are natural starting points because they already have established trading markets, price benchmarks, and regulated derivatives,” Jethani explained. “In my view, that makes them more workable assets to value, hedge, and sell than a thinly traded token whose quoted price may disappear when somebody needs to sell a meaningful holding.”

How Digital Assets Measure Up Under CFTC Capital Requirements

AssetMinimum Valuation HaircutRecognized Value per $1M Held12-Month Operating ReservesCash Liquidity Buffer
Bitcoin (BTC)20%$800,000EligibleIneligible
Ether (ETH)20%$800,000EligibleIneligible
Payment stablecoins2%$980,000EligibleIneligible
Non-readily marketable tokens100%$0IneligibleIneligible

Source: CFTC staff advisory, Nov. 23, 2026. Recognized values are illustrative and reflect the minimum prescribed valuation haircuts. The advisory applies to proprietary operating reserves, not customer margin or clearinghouse default funds.

The advisory applies strictly to an entity’s own operating reserves rather than customer margin or clearinghouse default funds. In releasing the guidance, the agency also underscored its legal limits:

“The advisory represents the views of staff only. It does not create new rules or enforceable rights, nor is it a no-action position and does not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission.”

Following the release, CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig welcomed the staff’s effort to provide greater clarity for digital assets in U.S. derivatives markets. Despite its non-binding status, Jethani described the guidance as “a meaningful step towards treating crypto as part of the financial resources of market infrastructure, with an explicit price attached to its risks.”

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Coinkite disclosed how a software error left Coldcard users’ Bitcoin recovery phrases vulnerable to hackers, South Korea moved to tighten oversight of stablecoin issuers and crypto exchanges, and 42 Macro warned that persistent inflation and further monetary tightening could put additional pressure on Bitcoin.

Coldcard reveals how Bitcoin wallet flaw went undetected for over 5 years

Bitcoin hardware wallet maker Coinkite has detailed how a security flaw in its Coldcard devices went undetected for more than five years despite several independent security reviews, including those using artificial intelligence (AI).

In a Nov. 23 postmortem report, Coinkite said that while its security checks confirmed the wallets had the correct system for generating secure recovery phrases, the company never verified whether the wallets were actually using it. As a result, a software error caused the wallets to use a weaker system instead, making the recovery phrases easier for hackers to guess.

A Bitcoin hardware wallet is a physical device that stores private keys offline, while a recovery phrase is a series of words that allows users to restore access to their funds if the device is lost or damaged.

Coinkite said at least 15 independent security reviews and research efforts failed to catch the flaw before the thefts began. It added that the weaker system went undetected because the recovery phrases looked normal and could still pass some security tests.

The flaw allowed hackers to steal at least 1,789 Bitcoin (BTC), worth around $114.7 million at the time of the thefts, Galaxy Research reported in August. Coinkite said it fixed the flaw on July 31 and introduced further security measures in August.

South Korea proposes bank-led stablecoins, 20% cap on crypto exchange stakes

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) unveiled a draft bill Tuesday that would initially limit issuance of won-denominated stablecoins to groups majority-owned by banks and generally cap shareholders’ stakes in crypto exchanges at 20%.

Banks would have to own more than half of a stablecoin issuer collectively, though a fintech or technology company could be its largest individual shareholder, the FSC said in its announcement.

Domestic stablecoin issuers would need FSC authorization and at least 5 billion won (about $3.7 million) in equity capital. They would also have to hold reserves covering at least 100% of their outstanding tokens and redeem them at face value without delay.

Exchanges would need dealing, brokerage and custody licenses and would have to meet capital and operating requirements. Shareholders’ stakes would be capped at 20%, or 34% with FSC approval.

The draft also seeks to lift South Korea’s 2017 ban on domestic initial coin offerings.

Why 42 Macro says it’s waiting to buy the Bitcoin dip

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, says his firm has trimmed its Bitcoin exposure and is waiting for signs that the sell-off has run its course before it considers buying again.

“We’ve already de-risked out of Bitcoin,” Dale said in an interview with Cointelegraph last week. “Our stress levels are low. We’re just waiting to buy.”

Dale’s comments came just days before Bitcoin fell to a two-year low around $55,100 on Saturday, raising questions about whether Bitcoin has finally found its bottom this cycle.

However, Dale warned that persistently high inflation could prompt further Fed tightening that could drain the liquidity that supports Bitcoin. The US Federal Reserve is widely expected to increase rates by 25 basis points at its next meeting on Dec. 9.

“Bitcoin doesn’t generate earnings. Bitcoin needs liquidity to go up,” he said.

Bitcoin was trading at around $64,000 at the time of the interview. Dale said it could fall another 30% to 40% if the S&P 500’s decline from its Oct. 6 peak reaches 20% by Christmas, which would put it at around $38,400. The S&P500 is currently down 7.4% from that peak.

summary: Authorities from 11 countries worked with Binance, Coinbase and Chainalysis to trace financial transactions and disrupt illegal streaming services.
content:
Law enforcement authorities from 11 countries, working with crypto exchanges Binance and Coinbase and blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, have traced more than 26 million euros ($28.5 million) in cryptocurrency transactions and disrupted 57 illegal streaming services in an operation coordinated by Europol, the law enforcement agency of the European Union.

In a Tuesday announcement, Europol said the five-day operation took place in Seville, Spain, from Nov. 16 to Nov. 20 and identified 321 websites illegally offering copyrighted content, attracting more than 7.3 million annual visits combined.

Europol said illegal streaming operators often collect subscription payments in cryptocurrency, allowing them to transfer funds quickly across borders. Investigators traced blockchain transactions to identify links between streaming services, cryptocurrency wallets and the individuals controlling them.

The EU’s law enforcement agency said the operation reflects a shift from focusing solely on shutting down illegal streaming services to also targeting the financial infrastructure behind them. The findings will support ongoing national investigations, including efforts to identify suspects and trace assets linked to criminal activity.

According to figures from the Audiovisual Anti-Piracy Alliance cited by Europol, an estimated 60 million people across Europe use unauthorized internet protocol television (IPTV) services, with estimated annual losses of 4.83 billion euros ($5.3 billion) for legitimate providers and a further 1.08 billion euros ($1.18 billion) in unpaid taxes for governments.

Related: Tron and Tether bring in Chainalysis after T3 crime unit folds

Europol targets international cybercrime networks

The operation follows other international efforts to disrupt criminal networks and their financial infrastructure. In March, US and European authorities dismantled SocksEscort, a malicious proxy service that enabled crimes including bank fraud and cryptocurrency account takeovers.

The service allowed customers to pay anonymously in cryptocurrency and received at least $5.7 million in user payments, according to investigators. Authorities froze about $3.5 million in cryptocurrency linked to the operation.

Earlier that month, Europol and the FBI took down LeakBase, a cybercrime forum with more than 142,000 registered users. An earlier cybercrime marketplace, RaidForums, had previously hosted leaked personal data belonging to users of crypto hardware wallet provider Ledger.

title: Researchers Unveil Encryption Breakthrough With Major Implications for Bitcoin
summary: Researchers from Stanford University and Byzantine Research have introduced Praxis, a witness encryption scheme designed to make a once-impractical cryptographic technique accessible on ordinary computers. It potentially enables Bitcoin bridges, conditional payments, and sophisticated smart contract...
content:
Researchers from Stanford University and Byzantine Research have introduced Praxis, a witness encryption scheme designed to make a once-impractical cryptographic technique accessible on ordinary computers. It potentially enables Bitcoin bridges, conditional payments, and sophisticated smart contracts without modifying the network’s consensus rules.

Key Takeaways

  • Stanford and Byzantine Research introduced Praxis on Nov. 23, 2026, addressing a cryptographic challenge dating back to 2013.
  • Praxis reduces ciphertext size and encryption costs by more than ten orders of magnitude compared with an earlier construction.
  • The technology could enable Bitcoin bridges without operators or challengers, although independent scrutiny and technical limitations remain.

Praxis Brings a 13-Year-Old Cryptographic Ambition Within Reach

A longstanding ambition in cryptography could open an entirely new chapter for Bitcoin, allowing complex spending conditions to be enforced without asking the network itself to verify them.

On Monday, Nov. 23, Stanford University professor and Babylon Bitcoin staking protocol co-founder David Tse, alongside Byzantine Research colleagues Nikhil Vanjani and Psi Vesely, introduced a research paper titled “Praxis: Practical Witness Encryption for NP.”

The paper was published through the International Association for Cryptologic Research (IACR). The researchers describe Praxis as the first witness encryption construction for general nondeterministic polynomial-time (NP) statements that combines broad applicability, practical computational costs, and mathematical security guarantees under specified assumptions.

First introduced in 2013 by Sanjam Garg, Craig Gentry, Amit Sahai, and Brent Waters, witness encryption reverses the conventional relationship between encrypted information and cryptographic keys. Rather than encrypting a message for someone who already possesses a particular key, the sender encrypts information against a mathematical statement.

Anyone possessing evidence that satisfies the statement can decrypt the message. That evidence, known in cryptography as a witness, could establish that a payment occurred, a computation was executed correctly, or a blockchain reached a predetermined length.

The person encrypting the message need not know who will eventually decrypt it, nor must that person remain available to authorize its release. “A ciphertext carries its own release condition, with no key to distribute and no party trusted to release the message,” the researchers explain.

Historically, however, general-purpose witness encryption has confronted a stubborn mathematical obstacle. Earlier constructions were either prohibitively expensive, restricted to particular applications, or dependent on cryptographic assumptions that subsequently came under attack.

For more than a decade, cryptographers struggled to reconcile three essential characteristics: general applicability, mathematical security guarantees, and practical computational requirements. Praxis is presented as the first construction to bring all three together.

From 110 Billion GiB to Just 7.88 GiB

Praxis dramatically narrows the distance between theoretical cryptography and practical engineering. At the 100-bit security level, the researchers’ construction produces a ciphertext measuring 7.88 gibibytes (GiB). Encryption requires approximately 20 billion base-field multiplications, while decryption with a valid proof requires an average of 8.6 billion.

Although those numbers appear substantial, the researchers estimate that both processes can be executed within seconds on a laptop. Encryption requires approximately 12 GB of memory, while decryption requires about 5 GB when the ciphertext is streamed rather than stored entirely in memory.

By comparison, an earlier witness encryption construction published by researchers Hair and Sahai in 2026 requires more than 110 billion GiB for a comparable task. Praxis reduces ciphertext size and encryption costs by more than ten orders of magnitude, while reducing decryption costs by more than six orders of magnitude, according to the paper’s comparative analysis.

The construction achieves these improvements partly by restructuring how mathematical information is represented, replacing enormous matrices with substantially smaller components that can be combined through cryptographic pairings.

Praxis also deliberately trades conventional polynomial-time decryption for a bounded search that remains computationally manageable at the selected security parameters. The researchers establish security within the bilinear generic group and random oracle models under a lattice-based mathematical assumption known as Module-SIS.

Moreover, the team provides machine-checked mathematical proofs written in Lean 4, a formal verification system, covering correctness and extraction at the construction’s specified parameters.

Praxis employs Groth16, a succinct cryptographic proof system, alongside the BN254 elliptic curve. One fixed verification key accommodates every NP relation, allowing increasingly elaborate release conditions to be expressed without increasing the ciphertext size under the proposed implementation.

The researchers explain that users could even encrypt information against conditions expressed through programs written in Rust.

Why Witness Encryption Could Fundamentally Change Bitcoin Bridges

For Bitcoin, the significance of Praxis lies in what the network could potentially accomplish without expanding its native scripting capabilities.

Bitcoin’s scripting language is deliberately limited, making the direct verification of sophisticated cryptographic proofs difficult. Developers seeking to introduce more expressive applications have consequently explored alternative mechanisms for verifying computations performed outside the blockchain.

BitVM, introduced by Robin Linus in 2023 and now in version 2, opened one such avenue. BitVM-style constructions employ interactive verification mechanisms through which dishonest computations can be challenged. Such arrangements generally depend on at least one honest participant being available to contest fraudulent activity.

Witness encryption introduces a fundamentally different proposition. Rather than requiring Bitcoin to verify a complex computation, developers could encrypt the cryptographic material necessary to spend bitcoin against a statement establishing that the computation was completed correctly.

Consider a Bitcoin bridge connecting the network to another blockchain. A withdrawal could be conditioned on the existence of a valid cryptographic proof establishing that the corresponding assets were properly withdrawn or destroyed on the other network.

A participant possessing the necessary proof could decrypt the spending material. Bitcoin would then process the resulting transaction using its existing consensus rules, without directly evaluating the underlying computation.

Linus, responding to the research, said that if the construction withstands independent peer review, then it “will fundamentally improve Bitcoin bridges. Eliminating the need for operators and making deposits and withdrawals non-interactive.”

Crypto researcher Eric Wall offered an equally enthusiastic, albeit conditional, assessment, suggesting that “Bitcoin might be technologically saved after all.”

Potential applications extend considerably beyond blockchain bridges. Witness encryption could facilitate cross-chain atomic swaps, private auctions, time-locked payments, and Bitcoin covenants, which impose restrictions on how funds may subsequently be spent.

For example, access to a bitcoin payment could be restricted to someone capable of proving that a corresponding stablecoin payment occurred. The release condition would be enforced through cryptography rather than through an intermediary overseeing the exchange.

Such mechanisms could furnish developers with considerably greater flexibility when designing Bitcoin applications, particularly those that rely on elaborate conditions the network’s existing scripting language cannot directly evaluate.

Praxis Still Faces Trusted Setup and Storage Hurdles

Despite the considerable efficiency gains, Praxis remains a research construction rather than a production-ready solution. The Groth16 implementation requires an honest trusted setup. If the secret randomness generated during that setup is retained, someone possessing it could fabricate proofs and decrypt ciphertexts associated with the corresponding verification key.

Consequently, eliminating ongoing bridge operators does not automatically eliminate every element of trust from the broader system. The 7.88 GiB ciphertext also presents practical challenges. Although manageable for modern computers, it remains unsuitable for direct inclusion in Bitcoin transactions. Applications would require dependable off-chain storage, distribution mechanisms, and assurances that encrypted information remains accessible when participants need it.

Nor should Praxis be confused with a quantum-resistant encryption system. Although Module-SIS belongs to a family of lattice-based problems studied in post-quantum cryptography, the construction also depends on pairing-based cryptography and its associated classical security assumptions.

The newly published paper has yet to undergo formal peer review, and its concrete security parameters, computational estimates, and implementation requirements warrant further independent examination.

Nevertheless, Praxis presents Bitcoin developers with an intriguing architectural possibility: expanding what bitcoin payments can accomplish without expanding what Bitcoin nodes must compute. If the construction survives independent scrutiny and its engineering limitations prove manageable, then witness encryption could furnish Bitcoin with capabilities previously pursued through consensus modifications or intermediary-dependent infrastructure. The most consequential innovation may ultimately reside outside the blockchain itself.

title: How to Stay Safe When Trading Online: 7 Practical Security Tips
summary: Online trading makes it easier than ever to manage investments. You can check market movements, place trades, and review your portfolio from almost anywhere.
content:
Skip to content

Online trading makes it easier than ever to manage investments. You can check market movements, place trades, and review your portfolio from almost anywhere.

But that convenience also comes with security risks.

A convincing phishing email, a weak password, or an unfamiliar trading platform can put your account and personal information at risk. And when real money is involved, even a small mistake can have serious consequences.

The good news is that improving your online trading security doesn’t require advanced technical knowledge. A few practical habits can make a meaningful difference.

Here are seven ways to protect your accounts, financial information, and devices when trading online.

1. Choose a Trading Platform You Can Trust

Before opening an account or depositing money, take some time to research the platform you’re considering.

A professional-looking website doesn’t necessarily mean a company is legitimate. Fraudulent trading platforms can have polished designs, realistic market charts, and customer support teams that appear convincing.

Start by checking whether the company is registered or authorized by the appropriate financial regulator in your country.

Don’t rely entirely on the information displayed on the platform’s website. Visit the regulator’s official website and search for the company’s name yourself.

It’s also worth reviewing a few practical details:

  • Account security: Does the platform offer two-factor authentication and login notifications?
  • Withdrawal policies: Are the requirements, processing times, and fees clearly explained?
  • Customer support: Can you contact the company through an official, verifiable channel?
  • Company information: Does the platform provide clear details about the business operating it?
  • User feedback: Are there repeated complaints about unexpected charges, account restrictions, or withdrawal problems?

Be particularly careful with platforms promising guaranteed profits or unusually high returns.

Financial markets involve risk, and legitimate providers should be transparent about it.

2. Strengthen Your Account Login Security

Your trading account may contain more than your investments. It can also store your name, contact details, identity documents, and banking information.

That makes account security especially important.

The network you use to access your account matters, too. If you sometimes check your investments over shared Wi-Fi, a free option from X-VPN can encrypt traffic between your device and the VPN server, adding privacy to your connection. However, it won’t protect against phishing websites or stolen passwords.

Start with a strong, unique password. Avoid reusing a password from your email, social media, or other financial accounts.

Next, enable two-factor authentication (2FA).

This adds another verification step when you sign in. Depending on the platform, you might approve a notification, enter a code from an authenticator app, or use a passkey.

An authenticator app is generally a better choice than SMS when both are available, since text messages can be vulnerable to certain account takeover attacks.

You should also check whether your trading platform supports login alerts. These notifications can help you identify an unfamiliar sign-in before someone makes changes to your account.

One final habit is easy to overlook: never share authentication codes with anyone, even if they claim to work for customer support.

Legitimate support staff should not need your password or one-time login code.

3. Learn to Recognize Trading Scams and Phishing Attempts

Not every online security threat involves sophisticated software.

Sometimes, an attacker simply needs to convince you to click a link.

Imagine receiving an email that appears to come from your trading platform. It warns that unusual activity has been detected and asks you to verify your identity immediately.

The message includes a button leading to what looks like the official login page.

You enter your username and password, only to discover later that the website was fraudulent.

This is a common phishing technique.

Attackers often create a sense of urgency to stop people from checking the details carefully.

Watch out for messages that:

  • Claim your account will be suspended unless you act immediately.
  • Ask you to confirm passwords, authentication codes, or payment information.
  • Direct you to unfamiliar websites that imitate legitimate trading platforms.
  • Promise special investment opportunities requiring immediate payment.
  • Arrive unexpectedly through messaging apps or social media.

If you’re unsure whether a message is genuine, don’t use its links.

Instead, open your trading platform through its official app or a bookmark you created earlier.

You can then check for account notifications or contact customer support directly.

Also remember that a website using HTTPS isn’t automatically trustworthy. Fraudulent websites can use encrypted connections too.

Checking the actual website address and the source of a message matters just as much.

4. Use Secure Internet Connections When Trading

It’s common to check market prices or manage investments while traveling, commuting, or working outside the office.

However, not every internet connection deserves the same level of trust.

Public Wi-Fi networks in cafés, hotels, and airports can be convenient, but it’s important to verify that you’re connecting to the correct network.

Someone could create a wireless network with a name similar to the official one, hoping visitors will connect without noticing the difference.

Before joining a shared network, confirm its name with the business or venue.

When possible, use your personal mobile connection for sensitive financial activities.

It’s also important to check that you’re using the official trading app or website before entering any account information. Avoid signing in through unfamiliar links, even when the network itself appears trustworthy.

These precautions are especially useful when managing investments away from home.

Keep in mind that a VPN doesn’t protect you from fraudulent websites, stolen passwords, or investment scams. You still need to verify where you’re signing in and follow your platform’s security recommendations.

It’s also worth checking that you’re using the official trading app or website before entering any account information.

These precautions are especially useful when managing investments away from home.

5. Keep Your Devices and Trading Apps Updated

Your trading account can be well protected, but an outdated device may still create security problems.

Software updates often include fixes for vulnerabilities that attackers could otherwise exploit.

This applies to your operating system, web browser, trading apps, and other software you use regularly.

For example, if a browser has an unpatched security vulnerability, visiting a malicious website could expose your device to unnecessary risk.

Keeping everything updated reduces your exposure to known problems.

A few habits can help:

  • Enable automatic updates: Let your device install important security fixes when they’re available.
  • Download apps from trusted sources: Use official app stores or links provided by the trading platform.
  • Remove unused extensions: Browser extensions may have access to information on the pages you visit, depending on their permissions.
  • Lock your devices: Use a strong passcode, fingerprint, or facial recognition.
  • Avoid unfamiliar downloads: Be cautious with files advertised as trading tools, market indicators, or account verification software.

Be especially careful with applications promoted through unsolicited messages.

A tool promising to improve your trading results may actually be designed to steal login information or install unwanted software.

If you use the same computer for work, entertainment, and investing, keeping your software organized and updated becomes even more important.

6. Protect Your Personal and Financial Information

Opening a trading account often requires personal identification and financial details.

Depending on the provider and local regulations, you may be asked to submit your address, identification documents, or bank account information.

These requirements can be legitimate, but the information should only be submitted through verified channels.

Before uploading sensitive documents, make sure you’re using the platform’s official website or app.

Avoid sending identification photos, bank statements, or payment details through personal messaging accounts unless you’ve independently verified the request and the channel is appropriate.

You should also be thoughtful about what you share publicly.

For example, posting screenshots of your trading dashboard might reveal account balances, transaction references, or other information you didn’t intend to disclose.

Even small details can become useful to scammers when combined with information from other sources.

Another important step is separating your financial accounts from everyday online activity.

Consider using a dedicated email address for banking and trading services. This can make legitimate account notifications easier to recognize and reduce the number of places where your financial login details are exposed.

It’s not a substitute for strong authentication, but it can make your accounts easier to manage securely.

Finally, avoid storing sensitive account documents in unprotected shared folders or leaving them accessible on devices used by other people.

7. Monitor Your Account for Unusual Activity

Security doesn’t end after you’ve created a strong password and enabled authentication.

It’s equally important to notice when something changes.

Make a habit of reviewing your trading account activity, especially after receiving an unexpected notification.

Look for unfamiliar login sessions, changes to contact information, new withdrawal instructions, or transactions you don’t recognize.

Some platforms provide a record of devices and locations associated with recent logins.

If that information is available, review it occasionally and sign out of sessions you no longer use.

You can also enable account alerts for important activities, such as:

  • New sign-ins or password changes.
  • Withdrawal requests.
  • Changes to linked payment methods.
  • Unusual account activity.

These alerts won’t prevent every incident, but they can help you respond sooner.

If you notice something suspicious, access the platform directly through its official website or app rather than following links in a notification.

Change your password if necessary, review active sessions, and contact the platform’s security team.

If you suspect your banking information has been compromised, contact your bank through its official support channels as well.

Acting quickly can help limit further unauthorized activity, although the available protections and recovery options depend on the platform and circumstances.

Make Online Trading Security Part of Your Routine

Staying safe while trading online isn’t about finding one tool that solves every security problem.

It’s about building habits that work together.

Choosing trustworthy platforms helps reduce your exposure to fraudulent services. Strong authentication makes account takeovers more difficult, while regular updates and careful browsing reduce common device and phishing risks.

Secure internet connections and account monitoring add further protection, especially if you frequently manage investments from different locations.

You don’t need to change everything at once.

Start by reviewing your current trading accounts. Check your authentication settings, update any reused passwords, and make sure important account notifications are enabled.

Then keep these security practices in mind whenever you trade.

A few minutes spent on prevention can save you considerable trouble later.

title: Utah moves to dismiss criminal charges against Kalshi after trading halt
summary: Utah’s attorney general warned that the criminal charges could be refiled if Kalshi resumes operations in the state, while separate civil litigation remains unresolved.
content:
Utah’s attorney general has moved to dismiss 14 criminal charges against prediction market platform Kalshi and its two co-founders after the company blocked users in the state from accessing its services.

The attorney general’s office said it filed a motion Monday to dismiss the case without prejudice in Utah’s Third District Court, allowing prosecutors to refile the charges if Kalshi resumes operations in the state.

The office opened a criminal investigation into Kalshi in September and filed charges on Oct. 28, alleging that the company offered illegal gambling to Utah residents. Kalshi subsequently agreed to block access to its platform in the state and monitor attempts to reach its services from Utah-based IP addresses.

“Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges,” Attorney General Derek Brown said, adding that his office would continue to enforce state gambling laws against other prediction market operators.

The office also sent cease-and-desist letters to several of Kalshi’s competitors, with six other prediction market companies agreeing to stop operating in Utah.

Kalshi General Counsel Yaakov Roth said in a Tuesday post on X that “good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized,” adding that the company was willing to work with state attorneys general while courts resolve the regulatory dispute.

Source: Yaakov Roth

The case is separate from a civil lawsuit Utah brought against Kalshi and its market-making partner Susquehanna International Group on Oct. 20, seeking restitution, damages and the recovery of proceeds from allegedly illegal gambling activities. The complaint estimates that Kalshi collected between $30.6 million and $61.2 million in fees from Utah-based accounts as of Oct. 19.

The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) announced its own lawsuit against Utah on Oct. 27, seeking to block the state from enforcing its gambling laws against federally regulated prediction markets. The lawsuit is part of a broader legal battle over the regulation of prediction markets, with the CFTC asserting exclusive jurisdiction over event contracts. The federal regulator has sued at least 12 states over the issue.
