title: Utah Moves to Drop Criminal Charges Against Kalshi, Founders After State Exit
summary: Utah prosecutors are seeking to dismiss criminal charges against prediction market operator Kalshi and its co-founders after the company blocked access to its platform in the state, marking a significant development in the escalating fight between state and federal authorities over the regulation of...
content:
Utah prosecutors are seeking to dismiss criminal charges against prediction market operator Kalshi and its co-founders after the company blocked access to its platform in the state, marking a significant development in the escalating fight between state and federal authorities over the regulation of prediction markets.

Key Takeaways

  • Utah is seeking to dismiss all 14 criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders after the prediction market operator blocked access in the state.
  • Seven prediction market operators have now agreed to withdraw from Utah, with authorities warning that criminal charges could be reinstated if Kalshi returns.
  • The move comes amid an escalating legal battle between state authorities and federal regulators over jurisdiction of prediction markets and sports event contracts.

The Utah Attorney General’s Office announced Tuesday that it had filed a motion in the Third District Court on Monday to dismiss all 14 criminal charges without prejudice, allowing prosecutors to revive the case should Kalshi resume operations in the state.

Kalshi agreed to implement geographic restrictions following the filing of criminal charges in October. The company also committed to monitoring attempts to access its platform from Utah-based IP addresses, prompting prosecutors to reconsider their case.

“Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges,” Utah Attorney General Derek Brown said in a statement.

Utah is one of only two U.S. states that prohibit gambling in all forms. The attorney general’s office said seven prediction market operators, including Kalshi, have now agreed to withdraw from the state following enforcement efforts that also included cease-and-desist letters to competing platforms.

Brown’s office said it would continue monitoring prediction market operators for compliance and could pursue additional civil or criminal proceedings against companies suspected of facilitating sports betting in Utah.

Kalshi’s Criminal Case and the Federal Fight

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, Utah filed criminal charges against Kalshi, CEO Tarek Mansour, and COO Luana Lopes Lara on Oct. 28 following an undercover investigation in which a state investigator wagered on 12 sporting events through the platform.

The charges included 13 felony counts and one misdemeanor. Kalshi initially rejected the allegations, accusing Utah authorities of political overreach and expressing confidence that it would prevail in court.

Utah had already secured a significant legal victory against Kalshi in August, when a federal judge determined that federal commodities legislation did not supersede the state’s gambling restrictions on sports event contracts. An appeals court subsequently denied Kalshi’s request to temporarily halt enforcement.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and Department of Justice (DOJ) sued Utah in October, arguing that the federal regulator has exclusive authority over event contracts offered through registered derivatives exchanges.

That dispute has since expanded. Earlier this month, Arkansas became the 11th state sued by federal authorities over prediction market enforcement efforts, following a lawsuit from Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin accusing Kalshi of operating an illegal gambling business.

Kalshi’s withdrawal from Utah also comes amid mounting controversy over the CFTC’s position on geographic restrictions. On Nov. 5, the regulator issued an interpretation directing exchanges to remove certain state-level access restrictions or explain why they cannot comply. Nine Democratic senators subsequently urged CFTC Chairman Michael Selig to withdraw or suspend the directive, arguing that it conflicts with existing court rulings.

While Utah’s proposed dismissal would remove the immediate threat of criminal prosecution for Kalshi and its founders, it does little to resolve the broader jurisdictional dispute threatening the prediction market industry’s ability to operate nationwide.

Tuesday’s announcement did not address the status of the separate civil litigation involving Utah and federal regulators.

title: US Freezes Over $1 Billion in Crypto as Anti-Scam Campaign Targets 800+ Defendants
summary:
US prosecutors have taken action in more than 400 cases involving over 800 defendants since March, while State Department-supported investigations with Southeast Asian authorities have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency. 
In an enforcement update issued on 24 November the DO...
content:
2026-11-24T22:35:02.205+02:00

Tuesday, 24/11/2026 | 20:35 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • The crackdown includes SEC action against 39 entities accused of using false regulatory filings to appear as legitimate US investment advisers.
  • In one case, prosecutors allege XETA promised returns of up to 3,000% and a €100 million guarantee before diverting investor funds.

US prosecutors have taken action in more than 400 cases involving over 800 defendants since March, while State Department-supported investigations with Southeast Asian authorities have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency.

In an enforcement update issued on 24 November the DOJ stated that charges had been filed or unsealed against over 30 scam defendants in the previous month alone.

One of the areas of focus in the wider campaign is the targeting of offshore and cross border schemes which pretend to be regulated financial institutions or make false claims as to their regulatory status in order to gain the trust of investors.

🧵 1/6: Today, DOJ announced the LARGEST ANTI-SCAM SURGE IN HISTORY, that targeted over 800 defendants to protect Americans from fraud. The anti-scam surge was launched following @POTUS Trump's Executive Order directing a government-wide crackdown on predatory schemes. https://t.co/AyufjhsLSd

— U.S. Department of Justice (@TheJusticeDept) November 24, 2026

Targeting False Regulatory Credentials and $1B in Proceeds

The update also contained details of enforcement action by the SEC against operators who had been accused of falsifying their regulatory credentials.

Since March the SEC has brought enforcement actions against 39 entities who have been accused of filing false Forms ADV in order to appear to be legitimate US investment advisers.

On the asset-recovery front, the DOJ said investigations conducted with Southeast Asian authorities and supported by the State Department had helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency.

The Scam Center Strike Force had separately reported more than $1 billion under restraint in October, although the DOJ did not explain how the two figures overlap.

“The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning. We will continue prosecuting those who perpetrate these schemes and disrupting the activities of transnational criminal organizations before they reach American shores,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche.

However, freezing digital assets does not immediately return funds to victims. Prosecutors must still secure court forfeiture orders before restrained cryptocurrency can be distributed to defrauded investors.

Anatomy of a Pitch: The XETA Capital Indictment

Among the prosecutions highlighted in the update was an indictment of five people living in the US and UK over an alleged cryptocurrency scheme operated through XETA Capital LLC.

According to the indictment obtained in Ohio on 12 November, the defendants misappropriated tens of millions of dollars after pitching XETA tokens as a way for retail investors to access traditional finance investments generally reserved for high-net-worth clients.

The defendants claimed the investments were managed through GAXSYS Holding AG, which they presented as a London-based investment manager regulated in Switzerland.

They promised annual returns ranging from 15% to 3,000% and said a €100 million guarantee from GAXSYS protected investors’ principal against losses.

Federal prosecutors allege that the promised returns and guarantee were false and that the defendants misappropriated tens of millions of dollars for personal use. The indictment contains allegations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

US prosecutors have taken action in more than 400 cases involving over 800 defendants since March, while State Department-supported investigations with Southeast Asian authorities have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency.

In an enforcement update issued on 24 November the DOJ stated that charges had been filed or unsealed against over 30 scam defendants in the previous month alone.

One of the areas of focus in the wider campaign is the targeting of offshore and cross border schemes which pretend to be regulated financial institutions or make false claims as to their regulatory status in order to gain the trust of investors.

— U.S. Department of Justice (@TheJusticeDept) November 24, 2026

Targeting False Regulatory Credentials and $1B in Proceeds

The update also contained details of enforcement action by the SEC against operators who had been accused of falsifying their regulatory credentials.

Since March the SEC has brought enforcement actions against 39 entities who have been accused of filing false Forms ADV in order to appear to be legitimate US investment advisers.

On the asset-recovery front, the DOJ said investigations conducted with Southeast Asian authorities and supported by the State Department had helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency.

The Scam Center Strike Force had separately reported more than $1 billion under restraint in October, although the DOJ did not explain how the two figures overlap.

“The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning. We will continue prosecuting those who perpetrate these schemes and disrupting the activities of transnational criminal organizations before they reach American shores,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche.

However, freezing digital assets does not immediately return funds to victims. Prosecutors must still secure court forfeiture orders before restrained cryptocurrency can be distributed to defrauded investors.

Anatomy of a Pitch: The XETA Capital Indictment

Among the prosecutions highlighted in the update was an indictment of five people living in the US and UK over an alleged cryptocurrency scheme operated through XETA Capital LLC.

According to the indictment obtained in Ohio on 12 November, the defendants misappropriated tens of millions of dollars after pitching XETA tokens as a way for retail investors to access traditional finance investments generally reserved for high-net-worth clients.

The defendants claimed the investments were managed through GAXSYS Holding AG, which they presented as a London-based investment manager regulated in Switzerland.

They promised annual returns ranging from 15% to 3,000% and said a €100 million guarantee from GAXSYS protected investors’ principal against losses.

Federal prosecutors allege that the promised returns and guarantee were false and that the defendants misappropriated tens of millions of dollars for personal use. The indictment contains allegations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: Bitcoin Lender Ledn Moves US Clients Onshore With New Custody Accounts
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Lender Ledn Moves US Clients Onshore With New Custody Accounts
Bitcoin lender Ledn launched a US custody account that lets clients hold bitcoin, gold, stablecoins and dollars, with no trading fees and a 0.5% spread.
This post Bitcoin Lender Ledn Moves US Clients Onshore Wit...
content:
Bitcoin lender Ledn is moving beyond loans. The company launched Ledn Custody on Tuesday, a new account that lets eligible U.S. clients hold bitcoin, gold, stablecoins and U.S. dollars, and buy, sell and swap between them in one place, with no trading fees and a 0.5% spread.

Ledn says that spread makes buying bitcoin through its app about half the cost of a standard purchase on the most popular U.S. bitcoin apps. The launch also moves Ledn’s U.S. clients, previously served from its Cayman Islands entity, to a U.S. company with a U.S. custodian.

Ledn has lent against bitcoin since 2018 and has serviced more than $11 billion in loans. Until now, most of its U.S. clients bought their bitcoin elsewhere and moved it to Ledn to borrow against it. The new account brings that first purchase in-house, from buying through to borrowing.

Ledn takes on the big bitcoin apps

A standard bitcoin purchase on the most popular U.S. apps costs about 0.9% to 1.25% once trading fees and spread are included, according to Ledn’s own analysis of published fees from October. That puts Ledn in direct competition with the trading apps where many Americans buy their first bitcoin.

On a $1,000 purchase, that works out to about $5 at Ledn against $9 to $12.50 elsewhere. Clients can deposit dollars and hold them in the account, or use them to buy bitcoin, gold and stablecoins. BitGo describes the gold option as tokenized gold.

“What our clients want is to hold hard assets, whether that’s bitcoin, gold or stablecoins,” Ledn co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Mauricio Di Bartolomeo said. “Most people buy them in one place, keep them in another, and when they need cash, they sell. Now they can do all three in one account.”

He added that clients can borrow against their bitcoin instead of selling, “with gold to follow.”

Segregated custody and an onshore push

Assets in a Ledn Custody account are held for the benefit of each client by an independent qualified custodian, segregated from Ledn’s own assets and never lent out for interest. BitGo Bank & Trust, a unit of BitGo (BTGO), provides the custody and trading services behind the account.

The custody setup is a selling point for a lender that came through 2022. Ledn says it has returned every client’s collateral across two full market cycles, including the collapse that bankrupted Celsius, BlockFi and Voyager. The company has also published monthly loan book and proof of reserves data.

“We’ve spent eight years earning our clients’ trust as a lender,” Ledn co-founder and CEO Adam Reeds said. “If you’re going to be a financial services company, boring is a good thing. We want to be the reliable, stable place where people build their wealth, not a platform with a million features built for trading.”

The onshore move lines up with Washington’s message. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in May that crypto’s problems stem from “the wild, wild west offshore,” adding, “we got to bring it onshore.” The Clarity Act, the market structure bill he urged Congress to pass, stalled in the Senate in September.

Ledn is chasing a big market. More than 67 million Americans now own crypto, or about one in four U.S. adults, according to a May survey. Competition for bitcoin borrowers is also heating up, with Cross River Bank launching its first bitcoin-backed loans this week.

Ledn has leaned on the capital markets to fund its lending, selling $188 million in bitcoin-backed bonds in February. The custody account now gives the lender a way to win clients before they ever need a loan.

Ledn Custody accounts will roll out to eligible U.S. individual clients over the coming days. The company plans to add lending against gold and open more U.S. states in the coming weeks.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Prop Firm Payouts Near $2 Billion: 10 Best Prop Firms In 2026
summary: Key takeaways Tracked prop firm payouts are nearing $1.97 billion across 45 firms since October 2023, with more than $115 million recorded in November alone, according to Payout Junction. Payout totals show that payments occurred, not that the average trader is profitable after challenge fees, reset...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Tracked prop firm payouts are nearing $1.97 billion across 45 firms since October 2023, with more than $115 million recorded in November alone, according to Payout Junction.
  • Payout totals show that payments occurred, not that the average trader is profitable after challenge fees, resets and subscriptions.
  • A $100,000 futures account with a $3,000 maximum drawdown leaves very little room for error; compare loss allowances and profit targets, not account size.
  • Consistency rules, payout buffers, withdrawal caps and trailing drawdowns can stop a profitable trader from withdrawing.
  • The guide compares ten firms across forex, futures and crypto based on published rules, not firsthand testing. Payouts are never guaranteed.

Prop firm payouts are approaching the $2 billion mark, with data from Payout Junction showing nearly $1.97 billion in cumulative payments across 45 tracked firms since October 2023. More than $115 million has been recorded in November 2026 alone.

The figures offer a glimpse into how large the funded trading industry has become. But finding the best prop firms in 2026 requires looking at something payout leaderboards rarely tell you: what traders actually have to go through to get paid.

A $100,000 futures account with a $3,000 maximum drawdown gives a trader just $3,000 of room for error. Add consistency requirements, withdrawal caps and restrictions on trading strategies, and two accounts with identical advertised balances can offer very different trading conditions.

The industry is also expanding beyond its traditional forex and futures markets. New platforms are introducing prop trading for cryptocurrencies and tokenized stocks, giving traders access to a wider range of markets without having to commit the full advertised account balance themselves.

For this guide, we examine ten prop firms across forex, futures and cryptocurrency markets, looking beyond advertised profit splits to compare evaluation rules, trading conditions, costs and payout eligibility.

Editorial disclosure: This guide is based on published trading rules, product documentation and available payout data. Traders can lose their challenge fees, and most retail funded trading programs initially use simulated accounts. Receiving a payout is not guaranteed.

Best Prop Firms In 2026 At A Glance

Prop firm Markets Best suited to Main consideration
FTMO Forex and CFDs Traditional evaluation models Higher first-phase target
FundedNext CFDs and futures Variety of account models Different reward conditions
FundingPips Forex and CFDs Flexible payout preferences Strategy and consistency restrictions
The5ers Forex Longer-term account development Program-specific growth rules
Hola Prime CFDs and futures Platform choice Withdrawal fees and eligibility
Topstep Futures Structured futures trading Payout caps and loss limits
Tradeify Futures Choice of payout structure Permanent funded-plan selection
Take Profit Trader Futures Frequent withdrawals Funded account buffer
Lucid Trading Futures Flexible funded-stage rules Payout objectives and caps
HyroTrader Crypto Crypto-native trading Volatility and drawdown restrictions

The firms are grouped by their suitability for different trading styles rather than ranked by a single payout leaderboard.

Prop Firm Payouts Approach $2 Billion

According to Payout Junction’s November 24 data, approximately 1.19 million payout transactions have been matched to public blockchain records since October 2023.

The tracker covers 45 firms, although its figures do not necessarily represent all payments made by those businesses. Bank transfers and other payments outside its blockchain tracking coverage may not appear in the dataset.

November has already recorded roughly $115.5 million in tracked payments across more than 91,000 transactions.

These are substantial figures, but they need context.

A firm paying out $50 million does not necessarily offer a better opportunity than one paying out $5 million. The larger business could simply have more customers, higher fees or a larger number of accounts.

Chart by NewsBTC, data from Payout Junction, November 16–22, 2026. Tracked blockchain payments only.

Nor do the figures tell us how much traders collectively spent on challenges, resets and subscriptions before receiving those payouts.

Without that information, it is impossible to determine the industry’s aggregate profitability for traders.

Payout data is useful evidence that payments have occurred. It is not evidence that the average customer makes money.

That distinction matters when comparing the following firms.

1. FTMO — Best For Traditional Evaluation Traders

FTMO offers a conventional two-phase evaluation for traders who prefer clearly defined profit objectives and fixed overall loss limits.

Its two-step model requires a 10% profit target during the first phase and 5% during verification.

The maximum daily loss is 5% of the initial simulated capital, while the overall loss limit is 10%.

For a $100,000 evaluation, that translates into a $10,000 first-phase profit target and a $10,000 maximum overall loss allowance.

FTMO Trading Conditions

  • Evaluation: Two phases under its traditional model.
  • Profit targets: 10% and 5%.
  • Maximum daily loss: 5%.
  • Maximum overall loss: 10%.
  • Funded environment: Simulated trading under contractual reward conditions.

FTMO also offers a separate one-step model. Traders should not assume that its rules are identical to the traditional challenge.

The two-step structure may appeal to traders whose strategies require more breathing room than accounts with narrow trailing loss limits.

The first-phase target, however, requires meaningful performance relative to the allowed drawdown.

Pros

  • Conventional evaluation structure.
  • Clearly documented trading objectives.
  • Static overall loss allowance on the two-step model.
  • No minimum trading-days requirement on the subsequent two-step FTMO Account.

Cons

  • A 10% initial profit target can be demanding.
  • Restrictions differ between account types.
  • Challenge fees remain at risk if the trader breaches the rules.

Our view

FTMO is worth considering for traders with an existing, tested forex or CFD strategy. Its two-step structure is easier to assess mathematically than many trailing-drawdown alternatives, although that does not make it easy to pass.

2. FundedNext — Best For Account Model Variety

FundedNext operates across CFDs and futures, offering several routes to funded-style trading.

Its Stellar 2-Step model is particularly interesting for traders who want a traditional evaluation with relatively conventional risk limits.

The first phase requires an 8% return, followed by 5% in verification. Both phases apply a 5% daily loss limit and 10% maximum overall loss.

The published rules specify five minimum trading days per phase.

FundedNext Trading Conditions

  • Representative model: Stellar 2-Step.
  • Profit targets: 8% and 5%.
  • Maximum daily loss: 5%.
  • Maximum overall loss: 10%.
  • Minimum trading days: Five per evaluation phase.

The firm also offers alternative CFD challenge formats and futures evaluations.

One area worth examining is its performance reward policy. Reward frequency and eligibility can vary according to the option selected, with some routes requiring a specific number of profitable trading days.

This makes comparing the headline profit split alone insufficient.

Pros

  • Multiple routes across different markets.
  • Traditional two-step model with an 8% initial target.
  • Different reward arrangements.
  • Detailed online help documentation.

Cons

  • Rules vary considerably between products.
  • Some reward options impose additional profitable-day requirements.
  • Promotional benefits and account add-ons may change the total cost.

Our view

FundedNext’s strongest feature is choice. Its biggest complication is also choice. Traders should compare the funded-stage conditions of each product before deciding which evaluation to purchase.

3. FundingPips — Best For Traders Comparing Payout Options

FundingPips offers several evaluation models, including one-step, two-step and evaluation-free alternatives.

Its 2-Step Standard model requires an 8% profit target followed by 5% in verification.

The firm’s current documentation also confirms that the previous optional 10% first-phase target was discontinued on July 24, 2026.

FundingPips Trading Conditions

  • Representative model: 2-Step Standard.
  • Profit targets: 8% and 5%.
  • Maximum daily loss: 5%.
  • Maximum overall loss: 10%.
  • Additional conditions: Dependent on the selected reward cycle.

FundingPips is an example of why traders must pay attention to changes in prop firm rules.

Its Standard model documentation applies a 35% consistency condition to the on-demand reward cycle.

This means a trader who generates most of their profit during one unusually successful session could need additional trading before qualifying for a withdrawal.

That might suit a strategy producing relatively steady returns. It could be less suitable for traders whose profits are concentrated around a handful of strong market opportunities.

Pros

  • Multiple evaluation routes.
  • Different reward-cycle choices.
  • Competitive first-phase target on the Standard model.
  • Extensive model-specific documentation.

Cons

  • Certain withdrawal options have consistency conditions.
  • Strategy restrictions require careful review.
  • Older account descriptions may no longer reflect current rules.

Our view

FundingPips deserves consideration for its payout flexibility, but traders should examine the conditions attached to their preferred withdrawal cycle rather than choosing whichever option advertises the highest reward share.

4. The5ers — Best For Longer-Term Account Development

The5ers offers several forex-focused evaluation and account-development programs.

Its High Stakes program is built around a two-stage evaluation and subsequent growth opportunities.

The firm distinguishes between different versions of High Stakes, making it important to identify the exact account being purchased rather than relying on older comparisons.

The5ers Trading Conditions

  • Representative model: High Stakes.
  • Evaluation: Two phases.
  • Drawdown: Program and account-specific limits.
  • Account growth: Subject to published scaling conditions.
  • Withdrawal eligibility: Dependent on the funded program.

The appeal of The5ers is its focus on account development over time.

Traders who already have a strategy capable of producing steady returns may find growth-oriented programs more interesting than accounts designed primarily around rapid evaluations.

However, scaling opportunities should not be treated as guaranteed increases in accessible trading capital.

The trader must meet the conditions attached to the program, and trading restrictions continue to apply.

Pros

  • Programs designed around longer-term account development.
  • Published rules for growth and profitable trading days.
  • Forex-focused product selection.
  • Different evaluation structures.

Cons

  • Growth conditions can extend the time required to increase account size.
  • Different program versions complicate comparisons.
  • News-trading restrictions require attention.

Our view

The5ers is a reasonable candidate for patient forex traders who value gradual account development. Its suitability depends on the precise High Stakes version and the trader’s ability to satisfy its growth criteria.

5. Hola Prime — Best For Traders Seeking Platform Choice

Hola Prime offers multiple evaluation formats across forex, CFDs and futures.

Its 2-Step Prime challenge requires an 8% profit target during the first phase and 5% during the second, with at least three trading days in each phase.

The firm’s published schedules also differentiate risk limits according to account size.

Hola Prime Trading Conditions

  • Representative model: 2-Step Prime.
  • Profit targets: 8% and 5%.
  • Minimum trading days: Three per phase.
  • Maximum overall loss: Generally 10%, with 8% applying to the $200,000 tier.
  • Daily loss: Account-specific.

Hola Prime’s product range gives traders alternatives to the standard evaluation experience. However, account fees, platform access and withdrawal terms differ across models.

Its advertised challenge-fee refund also comes with conditions. Under the reviewed 2-Step Prime terms, the refund is distributed across the first four successful payouts rather than returned immediately upon passing.

That is an important detail for anyone calculating how much they need to earn before recovering their initial expenses.

Pros

  • Multiple forex and futures programs.
  • Broad platform selection across products.
  • Relatively short minimum evaluation period.
  • Published reference tables for account rules.

Cons

  • Larger accounts can carry tighter percentage-based loss limits.
  • Challenge-fee refunds require successful payouts.
  • Withdrawal charges and reward conditions vary.

Our view

Hola Prime is worth comparing if trading platform choice matters to you. Just remember that a fast payout-processing promise begins after a withdrawal becomes eligible, not necessarily after your first profitable trade.

6. Topstep — Best For Structured Futures Trading

Topstep is focused on futures trading through its Trading Combine and subsequent funded-account structure.

Unlike a traditional CFD evaluation, the maximum loss allowance is relatively small compared with the advertised account size.

Its published Trading Combine parameters include maximum loss limits of $2,000 for a $50,000 account, $3,000 for a $100,000 account and $4,500 for a $150,000 account.

Topstep Trading Conditions

Account size Maximum loss allowance
$50,000 $2,000
$100,000 $3,000
$150,000 $4,500

A trader purchasing the $50,000 option is not receiving $50,000 that can be lost while testing a strategy. The relevant initial risk allowance is $2,000.

After passing the Trading Combine, traders can progress to an Express Funded Account, which is a simulated funded-stage account.

Its payout policy includes conditions relating to withdrawal eligibility, payout limits and changes to the maximum loss threshold after withdrawals.

Pros

  • Dedicated futures trading environment.
  • Explicit dollar-based maximum loss limits.
  • Structured progression beyond the evaluation.
  • Extensive educational and support documentation.

Cons

  • Narrow loss allowances relative to advertised account balances.
  • Withdrawals can alter the account’s remaining risk cushion.
  • Evaluation and funded-stage conditions differ.

Our view

Topstep is worth considering for futures traders who prefer a structured environment. Anyone moving from forex prop trading should first understand how dollar-based trailing loss limits differ from percentage-based static drawdowns.

7. Tradeify — Best For Choosing A Funded Payout Structure

Tradeify offers futures evaluations with different routes into funded-stage trading.

Its Select evaluation does not impose a daily loss limit during the evaluation but does apply a consistency requirement.

After passing, traders choose between Select Flex and Select Daily payout policies.

Tradeify Trading Conditions

  • Representative model: Select.
  • Market: Futures.
  • Evaluation daily loss limit: None under the reviewed Select rules.
  • Evaluation consistency: Applicable.
  • Funded payout options: Select Flex or Select Daily.

The ability to select a payout arrangement is attractive because not every trader earns profits in the same way.

A trader producing relatively consistent daily returns may prefer a different structure from someone whose strategy depends on occasional larger moves.

However, the choice is permanent for that funded account, according to Tradeify’s official payout policy.

Changing to the alternative arrangement requires obtaining another qualifying account.

Pros

  • Choice of funded-stage payout arrangements.
  • No daily loss limit during the reviewed Select evaluation.
  • Dedicated futures trading.
  • Published explanations of account-specific withdrawal conditions.

Cons

  • Evaluation consistency requirements still apply.
  • Funded payout-policy selection is permanent.
  • Drawdown and withdrawal conditions must be compared separately.

Our view

Tradeify’s Select model is particularly interesting because it allows traders to choose how they want to approach withdrawals after evaluation. That flexibility is only valuable if the trader understands both options before selecting one.

8. Take Profit Trader — Best For Frequent Withdrawal Opportunities

Take Profit Trader offers futures trading programs built around an evaluation, a simulated PRO account and potential progression to a live-market PRO+ account.

The firm published updated plan information on November 23, 2026, making older descriptions of its account rules particularly important to recheck.

Its current product announcement describes three-day evaluations, frequent PRO withdrawals and no funded-stage consistency rule under the new plans.

Take Profit Trader Trading Conditions

  • Market: Futures.
  • Evaluation: Single phase.
  • Minimum evaluation period: Three trading days under the new plans.
  • Evaluation consistency requirement: 50%.
  • PRO withdrawal availability: Daily, subject to buffer requirements.
  • Funded-stage consistency: None under the new plans.

The buffer is the detail traders should examine most closely.

The firm allows eligible traders to withdraw profits above the required buffer. Consequently, a trader can have a profitable account without necessarily being able to withdraw all that profit while retaining the account.

Legacy accounts may also remain subject to their original terms.

Pros

  • Frequent withdrawal opportunities.
  • No funded-stage consistency condition under the reviewed new plans.
  • Single-phase futures evaluation.
  • A route to live-market trading through PRO+.

Cons

  • PRO buffer requirements must be satisfied.
  • Legacy and newer accounts can operate under different rules.
  • Futures-only product offering.

Our view

Take Profit Trader stands out for its withdrawal model. Traders interested in frequent payouts should still calculate how much profit must remain in the account before treating those earnings as spendable income.

9. Lucid Trading — Best For Flexible Funded-Stage Rules

Lucid Trading offers several futures account models, including LucidPro, LucidFlex, LucidDirect and LucidDaily.

Its LucidFlex program is particularly relevant to traders who want to avoid funded-stage profit-concentration restrictions.

According to the firm’s LucidFlex documentation, the funded account does not impose a consistency rule or a separate payout buffer.

The published profit-sharing arrangement is 90% for the trader.

Lucid Trading Conditions

  • Representative model: LucidFlex.
  • Market: Futures.
  • Funded-stage consistency: None.
  • Reward share: 90%.
  • Separate payout buffer: None.
  • Withdrawal eligibility: Subject to qualifying objectives and account rules.

The absence of a consistency rule does not mean traders can withdraw unrestricted amounts whenever they choose.

LucidFlex still has specific payout conditions, including requirements that must be satisfied before a withdrawal is approved.

Traders must also consider how a payout affects the account’s maximum loss threshold.

Pros

  • No funded-stage consistency rule on LucidFlex.
  • No separate payout buffer on that model.
  • 90% advertised reward share.
  • Multiple futures account structures.

Cons

  • Payout objectives continue to apply.
  • Withdrawal caps and qualifying conditions need examination.
  • Other Lucid products have different requirements.

Our view

LucidFlex may appeal to traders who dislike having their profitable sessions constrained by a consistency formula. That makes the account more flexible in one respect, not necessarily less risky overall.

10. HyroTrader — Best For Crypto-Native Prop Trading

HyroTrader focuses on cryptocurrency traders rather than adapting a traditional forex evaluation to include a limited selection of digital assets.

Its one-step program requires a 10% profit target, with a 4% daily drawdown and 6% maximum overall loss under the published model.

The firm also offers alternative evaluation formats, including its recently introduced lower-cost Hyro Core program.

HyroTrader Trading Conditions

  • Representative model: One-Step.
  • Market: Cryptocurrency.
  • Profit target: 10%.
  • Daily drawdown: 4%.
  • Maximum overall loss: 6%.
  • Standard minimum trading days: Five on the reviewed One-Step model.

The attraction is that traders can use crypto-oriented trading infrastructure and market data rather than relying exclusively on a conventional forex platform.

For traders unfamiliar with derivatives, our guide to long and short positions in crypto explains how leverage and liquidation affect market exposure.

HyroTrader’s trading rules also clarify that allocated challenge and funded-account balances are simulated. Payouts represent a contractual share of eligible simulated trading performance.

That distinction matters because the term funded account is frequently misunderstood.

Pros

  • Cryptocurrency-focused trading experience.
  • Multiple evaluation options.
  • Exchange-demo integration on supported setups.
  • Detailed risk and trading-rule documentation.

Cons

  • A 10% target against a 6% overall loss limit is demanding.
  • Cryptocurrency volatility can make tight loss limits difficult to manage.
  • Account-specific strategy and payout restrictions apply.

Our view

HyroTrader is worth examining for traders who already specialize in crypto markets. It is less compelling for someone whose only reason for choosing crypto is the belief that higher volatility makes a challenge easier to pass.

How The Best Prop Firms Compare By Trading Style

There is no single account structure that suits everyone.

Trading preference Firms worth comparing
Traditional forex evaluations FTMO, FundedNext
Lower first-phase profit targets FundingPips, FundedNext, Hola Prime
Account development and scaling The5ers
Flexible futures payout arrangements Tradeify
Frequent eligible withdrawals Take Profit Trader
No funded-stage consistency rule on selected models LucidFlex, Take Profit Trader
Structured futures evaluations Topstep
Crypto-focused trading HyroTrader
Variety of evaluation products FundedNext, Hola Prime, FundingPips

These selections reflect specific published product features, not independently measured payout approval rates or guarantees of superior results.

The Number Most Prop Traders Should Pay More Attention To

The advertised account balance is usually one of the least informative numbers in a prop firm comparison.

Consider two hypothetical accounts:

Trading condition Account A Account B
Advertised balance $100,000 $50,000
Profit target $6,000 $3,000
Maximum loss allowance $3,000 $5,000
Target divided by loss allowance 2.0 0.6

Account A offers twice the advertised balance of Account B. Yet it provides less room for losses and requires a substantially higher profit relative to that allowance.

This does not establish the probability of passing either challenge. That depends on the strategy, trading costs, risk management and other account rules.

It does show why choosing the largest advertised account is not always sensible.

The calculation becomes more complicated when an account uses trailing drawdown.

Static Vs. Trailing Drawdown

A static maximum loss threshold remains anchored to a specified balance under the account’s rules.

A trailing drawdown moves upward as the trader generates profits, potentially reducing the room available for a subsequent losing streak.

Intraday trailing drawdown is particularly important because some models adjust the threshold based on unrealized profits.

A trade that briefly gains $1,000 before closing with a much smaller profit can therefore affect the trader’s remaining loss allowance.

Two firms advertising the same maximum drawdown can offer very different practical conditions depending on how and when that threshold moves.

Why A Profitable Trader Can Still Miss Out On A Payout

Passing an evaluation is generally only the first stage.

The rules that determine whether someone receives a withdrawal can be more restrictive than the initial profit targets.

Consistency Requirements

A consistency rule limits how much of the qualifying profit can come from a single trading session or another defined period.

For example, suppose a trader earns $2,000 during their best day and finishes the payout cycle with $4,000 in qualifying profit.

That best day represents 50% of the total.

Under a hypothetical 40% consistency requirement, total qualifying profit would need to reach at least $5,000, assuming the best day remains unchanged and the rule uses this particular calculation.

The trader may have to continue trading even though they are already profitable.

Payout Buffers And Withdrawal Caps

Some firms require profits to remain in an account as a buffer against future losses.

Others limit how much traders can withdraw during their initial payout cycles.

These restrictions are not necessarily unreasonable. A firm may want traders to demonstrate sustained performance before allowing larger withdrawals.

But customers should know exactly what they are buying.

There is a considerable difference between advertising daily payouts and allowing a trader to withdraw every dollar earned that day.

Prohibited Trading Strategies

Account agreements can restrict copy trading, certain automated strategies, cross-account hedging, account sharing, news trading and other trading behaviors.

The precise definitions differ between firms.

Before paying for an account, traders should review both the public trading objectives and the account agreement governing payout eligibility.

A strategy permitted during evaluation may have different conditions after funding.

How Much Do Prop Firm Challenges Really Cost?

The advertised challenge price is only the initial expense.

Depending on the firm and product, customers may also incur subscription charges, reset fees, funded-account activation fees, market-data fees, platform costs or withdrawal-processing charges.

Promotional discounts can make the first purchase attractive without necessarily reducing the cost of subsequent attempts.

Consider a hypothetical trader who purchases four $100 challenges before successfully qualifying for a funded account. That trader has spent $400 before accounting for any additional charges.

The first $300 payout would not mean the trader has made a net profit from prop trading.

Their total challenge expenditure would still exceed their withdrawals.

This is another reason the industry’s approaching $2 billion payout milestone should not be confused with $2 billion in net trader earnings.

How We Selected These Prop Firms

Our editorial assessment considers the following factors:

  • Evaluation design: How the profit targets compare with the available loss allowance.
  • Drawdown mechanics: Whether thresholds are static, trailing, intraday or adjusted after withdrawals.
  • Payout eligibility: The conditions that must be met before traders can withdraw.
  • Cost transparency: Challenge fees, recurring charges, resets and other expenses.
  • Trading infrastructure: Supported markets, available platforms and product accessibility.
  • Rule transparency: Whether current trading restrictions and account agreements are readily available.
  • Account suitability: Which trading styles are compatible with each product.

The selection is based on documentary research rather than a claim that NewsBTC has personally purchased, traded or withdrawn money from every program.

Reported payouts are considered supporting evidence of industry activity, not a standalone measure of reliability.

Are Prop Firms Legitimate?

Retail prop firms generally offer traders access to an evaluation or simulated trading program in exchange for a fee.

Belgium’s financial regulator, the FSMA, has also published a consumer warning about retail prop trading programs, highlighting the risks of paying for repeated challenges.

Participants who meet the contractual requirements may receive monetary rewards linked to their trading performance. Some businesses subsequently move qualifying traders into live-market accounts.

This is different from opening a conventional brokerage account with personal deposited trading capital.

It also means traders should examine who operates the program, which legal entity they contract with, where disputes are handled and what happens if the provider changes its rules or ceases operations.

A large number of successful payout transactions does not guarantee that every valid withdrawal will be approved, nor does it establish the financial health of the company.

Before buying a challenge, traders should read the current agreement, establish their eligibility and understand which circumstances can lead to account termination.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Is The Best Prop Firm In 2026?

FTMO and FundedNext are worth comparing for traditional forex evaluations. Topstep, Tradeify, Take Profit Trader and Lucid Trading offer different futures trading structures, while HyroTrader is focused on cryptocurrency.

The most suitable firm depends on the trader’s strategy, risk tolerance, market preference and withdrawal requirements.

Which Prop Firms Have Daily Payouts?

Take Profit Trader offers daily eligible withdrawals under its reviewed PRO model, subject to the required buffer. Tradeify also offers a Select Daily payout arrangement.

Daily availability does not remove other eligibility conditions.

Which Prop Firms Have No Consistency Rule?

LucidFlex does not impose a funded-stage consistency rule under its published terms. Take Profit Trader’s new PRO plans also advertise no funded-stage consistency requirement.

Evaluation-stage restrictions may still apply.

What Is The Best Crypto Prop Firm?

HyroTrader is one of the crypto-focused firms worth researching because its programs are built around digital-asset trading.

Traders should compare cryptocurrency market access, drawdown calculations, exchange integrations and payout eligibility before selecting a program.

Can You Lose Money With A Prop Firm?

Yes. Traders can lose evaluation fees, subscriptions, reset fees and other charges without ever receiving a payout.

The simulated nature of many funded accounts does not eliminate the financial risk of paying for repeated evaluations.

Are Prop Firm Payouts Guaranteed?

No. Withdrawals depend on the firm’s contractual requirements, trading-rule compliance and ability to make payments.

Historical payout figures do not guarantee future withdrawals.

Final Verdict

The prop trading industry has grown considerably, and nearly $2 billion in tracked payouts demonstrates that substantial sums are changing hands.

What it does not demonstrate is how many traders are profitable after accounting for their expenses.

The best prop firm is not necessarily the one paying the most money, offering the largest account or advertising the highest profit split.

It is the one whose evaluation and funded-stage rules are compatible with a trader’s existing strategy.

Before purchasing a challenge, calculate how much room the account actually provides for losses, how much profit must be generated before a withdrawal becomes possible and how much repeated attempts could cost.

Those numbers are considerably more useful than the advertised account balance.

title: Bitcoin sell-off driven by weak demand, forced liquidations: 21Shares
summary: The crypto asset manager warned that Bitcoin’s downturn could persist amid weak investor demand, while forecasting an uneven recovery across crypto sectors.
content:
The $6.4 billion hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance in October triggered Bitcoin’s recent sell-off, but weakening investor demand and forced liquidations drove most of the subsequent losses, according to a Nov. 24 report from crypto asset manager 21Shares.

While the Oct. 29 hack triggered the initial decline, the report found that weakening demand drove Bitcoin (BTC) down a further 8.3% between Nov. 4 and Nov. 11. Forced selling of leveraged positions led to the steepest decline, sending BTC down another 13.5% over the next three days. Crypto liquidations totaled $5.8 billion in the week ending Nov. 15, with long positions accounting for 81%.

Bitcoin’s sell-off and leverage unwind. Source: 21Shares

Signs of weakening demand were also seen in the stablecoin supply, which contracted by $10.7 billion following the hack, marking the largest 18-day decline in dollar terms since the Terra collapse in 2022. US spot Bitcoin and Ether (ETH) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded combined outflows of $3.9 billion between Oct. 30 and Nov. 13.

Eliezer Ndinga, global head of research at 21Shares, told Cointelegraph that the market was already vulnerable before the hack:

The Fed had raised rates in September, core inflation had risen 0.3% for a third straight month, and doubts over AI spending had kept the Nasdaq-100 below its October 6 record. The hack started the sell-off, but bitcoin fell only 5.1% in the two days after it and had recovered almost all of that by November 4.

The report also found little evidence of selling by other major Bitcoin holders. The 18,270 BTC and 522,409 ETH stolen in the Binance hack remained unspent as of mid-November, while neither the US government nor the Mt. Gox trustee had transferred Bitcoin to exchanges since the attack.

Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy continued buying, adding 2,332 BTC between Oct. 26 and Nov. 15. Meanwhile, miner transfers to exchanges fell to their lowest levels since at least 2020, although the data may not capture sales by publicly traded mining companies.

Related: Bitcoin slides amid US tariff nerves as Anthropic falls below IPO price

21Shares sees a K-shaped recovery for crypto

21Shares believes Bitcoin is already more than a year into a cyclical bear market. Historically, such downturns have lasted about two and a half years and resulted in average price declines of 84%, according to the report.

However, the researchers see a low probability of Bitcoin revisiting the depths of previous bear markets, citing the growing presence of institutional investors and spot ETFs. Ndinga said the competitive landscape for crypto has also changed:

Crypto is also no longer the only frontier technology in investors’ minds, with AI and robotics drawing talent and capital away from it. We expect a K-shaped recovery, where bitcoin, 24/7 trading venues, privacy protocols and quantum-resistant solutions advance while other parts of the market lag.

Ndinga warned that a larger-than-expected Federal Reserve rate hike in December could prolong the downturn. Another potential source of selling pressure is the $2.2 billion in BTC and ETH stolen in the Binance hack, which could reach the market through over-the-counter (OTC) brokers in the coming months.

Ndinga identified Bitcoin’s realized price of $53,250, a measure of the average investor cost basis, as a key downside level to watch. Conversely, a return to the $73,000 to $75,500 range coupled with sustained ETF inflows and rising stablecoin balances would signal renewed investor demand.

Stablecoin supply changes following major market shocks. Source: 21Shares

title: Bitcoin Price Today: BTC Struggles to Hold $60K as Glassnode Flags Annual Hash Rate Decline
summary: Bitcoin (BTC) is struggling to maintain its position around $60,000 as weakening mining economics and rising realized losses add pressure to an already fragile market.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin (BTC) is struggling to maintain its position around $60,000 as weakening mining economics and rising realized losses add pressure to an already fragile market.

Glassnode data points to the first annual decline in Bitcoin’s mean hash rate since the 2021 China mining ban, highlighting growing stress across the mining sector.

BTC was trading near $60,051 at the time of writing. Technical indicators continue to show a bearish trend, while on-chain metrics reveal that investors are realizing losses at levels last observed during the 2022 FTX collapse. Together, these developments have put the $58,500 support region in focus as traders assess whether Bitcoin can stabilize or face another leg lower.

Bitcoin Tests $58,548 Support After Potential Bear Trap

Bitcoin’s recent price action has raised the possibility of a bear trap after a weekend decline briefly pushed the asset below an important technical level. However, Monday’s daily candle closed back above the breached region, suggesting that sellers failed to maintain control at that point.

BTC faced rejection at the Point of Control (POC) and is now retesting $58,548 support, reinforced by the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement and Value Area Low (VAL). Source: TradingView

The recovery has not yet produced a sustained bullish reversal. BTC subsequently faced rejection around the Point of Control (POC), a price level representing the highest trading activity within the selected range. The cryptocurrency has since returned to test support near $58,548.

According to a TradingView analysis, this region carries several technical confluences, including the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement and the Value Area Low (VAL). Their alignment makes $58,548 an important level for assessing whether buyers can defend the current trading range.

A sustained hold above this zone could improve the prospects of a recovery toward $65,519. That level represents a potential upside target within Bitcoin’s broader range-bound structure. However, a decisive breakdown below support would weaken the recovery setup and expose BTC to additional downside.

Trading volume and the daily closing price will remain important confirmation signals. A brief move below support followed by a quick recovery would present a different technical picture from a sustained breakdown accompanied by stronger selling activity.

Bitcoin Hash Rate Records First Annual Decline Since 2021

Bitcoin’s mining sector is showing signs of mounting pressure as lower market prices weaken the economics of operating mining equipment. Glassnode reports that Bitcoin’s 30-day mean hash rate has fallen approximately 8% below its level a year earlier, marking the first year-over-year contraction since the 2021 China mining ban.

Bitcoin miners are shutting down machines as the network’s hash rate falls 8% year over year, marking its first annual decline since China’s 2021 mining ban. Source: Glassnode via X

The decline contrasts with the network’s expansion during much of the intervening period. In 2021, China’s restrictions on cryptocurrency mining forced a substantial portion of global mining operations offline, triggering a sharp reduction in network computing power. The latest contraction, however, appears to have a different underlying cause.

Glassnode attributes the current weakness primarily to deteriorating mining profitability. With BTC trading around $60,000–$62,000, hash price has fallen to an all-time low, reducing the revenue miners generate relative to their computing capacity.

This pressure is encouraging operators to switch off older and less efficient machines. When mining revenue no longer covers electricity and operating expenses, keeping outdated equipment active becomes financially unsustainable. The resulting reduction in computing power is reflected in the network’s declining hash rate.

Hash rate measures the total computational power used by miners to process transactions and compete to add new blocks to the Bitcoin blockchain. Although short-term declines do not necessarily indicate a security problem, a prolonged contraction can highlight financial stress among mining operators.

The development also illustrates how Bitcoin’s market price influences the economics of its mining industry. Lower prices reduce the fiat value of block rewards and transaction fees, while operating expenses remain a significant burden. More efficient miners may continue operating, but less competitive facilities face greater pressure to reduce capacity or shut down.

Bitcoin Technical Indicators Maintain a Strong Sell Outlook

TradingView’s technical summary presents a broadly bearish picture for Bitcoin near $60,049. The overall indicator gauge records 15 sell signals, 10 neutral readings, and just one buy signal, reflecting the strength of the recent downward trend.

Moving averages account for most of the negative readings. The moving-average summary shows 14 sell signals, one neutral reading, and no buy signals. By comparison, oscillators remain more balanced, with nine neutral readings, one sell signal, and one buy signal.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands at 25, placing Bitcoin in oversold territory. Such a reading indicates that recent selling has been particularly intense, although it does not independently confirm that a price bottom has formed.

Other momentum indicators also reflect persistent weakness. The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) registers a sell signal at -4,806, while the Average Directional Index (ADX) stands at 49, indicating a strong prevailing trend. The Stochastic RSI Fast reads 47, while the Williams Percent Range is at -76.

The moving-average structure reinforces the bearish outlook. Bitcoin remains below its 10-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $62,635 and its 20-day EMA at $66,454. The 50-day EMA stands at $72,397, while the 200-day EMA is considerably higher at $74,799.

The Hull Moving Average (HMA), one of the closest short-term trend references, sits near $59,911 and also carries a sell signal. This suggests that the current price has yet to establish a convincing recovery above short-term trend indicators.

Classic pivot-point analysis identifies $58,181 as an important downside reference, close to the $58,548 support region highlighted by the TradingView analysis. On the upside, the nearest moving-average resistance cluster sits around $62,000–$68,000.

A recovery above this area would be necessary to improve the short-term technical picture. Until then, the broader trend remains under pressure, even as oversold readings leave room for temporary price stabilization.

Glassnode Flags Realized Losses at FTX-Era Levels

Bitcoin’s weakness is also visible in on-chain investor behavior. Glassnode reports that realized losses, measured against capital inflows over the previous year, have climbed to their highest levels since the 2022 FTX collapse.

The metric nearly doubled within a week as BTC retreated toward $60,000, indicating that investors are realizing substantially greater losses compared with the capital entering the market over the preceding year.

Historical spikes in realized losses have often aligned with Bitcoin price bottoms, although some preceded further declines, indicating that capitulation signals can vary in timing. Source: Glassnode via X

Realized losses occur when Bitcoin moves on-chain at a price below the level at which it was previously acquired. Unlike unrealized losses, which reflect declining portfolio values on paper, realized losses indicate that coins have changed hands at a lower valuation.

Historically, sharp increases in realized losses have sometimes appeared near major market lows, when investors sell during periods of heightened uncertainty. However, the indicator does not consistently identify the bottom. Similar spikes have also occurred earlier in prolonged bear markets, meaning further downside can follow elevated loss realization.

Glassnode’s latest findings also highlight Bitcoin’s relative weakness compared with broader financial markets and major technology stocks, including NVIDIA. The divergence adds another dimension to the current market downturn, as Bitcoin’s performance remains under pressure despite activity elsewhere in risk assets.

The combination of rising realized losses and declining mining profitability points to stress across two important parts of the Bitcoin ecosystem. Investors are locking in losses, while miners are facing lower returns and withdrawing less efficient computing capacity.

Bitcoin Price Outlook: Can BTC Defend $58.5K?

Bitcoin’s immediate direction largely depends on its ability to maintain support around $58,548. The level combines the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement with the Value Area Low, while the classic S3 pivot sits slightly lower at $58,181.

If buyers defend this region, BTC could attempt a recovery toward $65,519, although the moving-average cluster between $62,000 and $68,000 presents an important obstacle. A sustained move above these levels would provide stronger evidence that selling pressure is easing.

On the downside, a confirmed breakdown below $58,181 would weaken the current support structure. Traders would then need to assess lower price levels as Bitcoin searches for additional demand.

For now, the broader technical picture remains bearish. Oversold momentum indicators suggest that selling may be approaching extreme levels, but the moving averages, MACD, and ADX continue to favor the downside trend.

Glassnode’s latest on-chain observations add to the cautious outlook. The first annual hash rate decline since 2021 and realized losses reaching FTX-era levels indicate that the current correction is affecting both investors and mining operators.

Whether these conditions develop into a broader capitulation phase or precede a period of stabilization will depend on subsequent price action, mining activity, and changes in investor behavior. For Bitcoin, defending the $58,500 region remains a key near-term test.

title: Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients
Anchorage Digital is launching 61st Parallel Asset Management, a subsidiary expected to open by early December with a bitcoin-denominated fund that lets custody clients earn yield.
This post Anchorage Digital...
content:
Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin.

The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley said in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude.

“We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said.

Anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database showed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public.

Paperwork dating back to summer

The entity itself is not new. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware company, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan.

Anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively.

Anchorage has not said publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Those details matter to bitcoin holders, because bitcoin pays no interest on its own. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk.

Public companies have already tested some of those approaches. Trump Media disclosed this month that it had pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can rehypothecate, or reuse, the coins.

From custodian to full-service bank

Founded in 2017, Anchorage received a national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in January 2021, the first crypto firm to win one. The OCC lifted a 2022 consent order over the bank’s anti-money laundering controls in August 2025.

The bank no longer stands alone. Last December, the OCC granted conditional approvals to five more digital asset firms, including Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Paxos and Fidelity Digital Assets, to become national trust banks.

The asset manager is the latest in a run of expansions. On Nov. 5, Anchorage Digital Swap Dealer LLC applied to the National Futures Association to register as a swap dealer with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The company said much of its options growth has come from public companies holding bitcoin and ether on their balance sheets.

In February, Tether made a $100 million strategic investment in Anchorage at a $4.2 billion valuation, after picking Anchorage Digital Bank as the issuer of its U.S. stablecoin. Anchorage also ran its first employee tender offer at that valuation instead of raising new primary capital.

In June, the company rolled out off-exchange settlement with Binance, letting institutions trade on the exchange while their assets stay in segregated custody at the bank. Anchorage also offers trading, staking and settlement to institutional clients.

The swap dealer application remains under review by the National Futures Association, and McCauley said at the time that the company was not in a position to speculate on timing.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: FCA Proposes One Fee for Firms Applying for Payments and Crypto Approval
summary:
The FCA’s crypto authorisation window is already open, but a business applying for payments or e-money registration at the same time still has to pay two application fees.  The regulator now wants to charge only the higher one. 
What a Joint Application Costs 
Take a new business planning to offer p...
content:
2026-11-24T20:03:39.595+02:00

Tuesday, 24/11/2026 | 18:03 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • A firm applying for payments registration and crypto custody approval could pay £11,260 instead of £16,900.
  • Companies must pay both fees, if they apply now, but the FCA says it will refund the difference if the proposal is adopted.

The FCA’s crypto authorisation window is already open, but a business applying for payments or e-money registration at the same time still has to pay two application fees. The regulator now wants to charge only the higher one.

What a Joint Application Costs

Take a new business planning to offer payment services and crypto custody. At current FCA rates, a company planning to offer both payment services and crypto custody is supposed to pay £16,900 in fees: £11,260 for crypto application and £5,640 for payments. Under the new proposal, it would pay £11,260.

The idea is not new, as the FCA already applies similar bulk discounts when a firm applies for permissions under the Financial Services and Markets Act (FSMA) alongside registration under the UK's Money Laundering Regulations at the same time.

Now it wants to apply the same rule to payments or e-money applications filed together with a cryptoasset application. Each service would still require its own approval.

Firms Applying Now May Get a Refund

Crypto exchanges and wallet custodians currently register with the FCA under anti-money laundering rules. From 25 October 2027, activities including crypto custody will require authorisation under the UK’s new financial services regime.

The FCA started accepting applications under the new regime on 30 September 2026, but its proposed single fee for firms also applying for payments or e-money registration is still under consultation. Those firms must pay both fees for now.

If the rule is adopted, the FCA says it will refund the difference, saving firms up to £5,640, the highest fee tier for payment and e-money registrations. However, the actual saving will depend on the specific permissions each applicant seeks.

Overall, the regulator expects the single-fee rule to benefit up to 40 applicants, including early filers eligible for a refund.

A Separate Change to Annual Fees

The proposal also deals with what firms pay when they surrender their FCA authorisation. A firm applying to withdraw a permission currently pays the full annual fee for that year regardless of when the application is made (so if it's an April application it still pays the full annual fee).

The FCA proposes a 25% charge for applications made from April to June, with that percentage increasing each quarter to 100% for applications made from January to March.

The regulator wants to launch the new annual fee schedule on 1 April 2027. If their systems aren't ready then it would be a year later. The consultation closes 19 January 2027 and the initial crypto application window closes 28 February.

Businesses who are filing their payments and crypto applications prior to the FCA settling the fee rule will need to budget for both charges. Any refund will be subject to the final outcome of the rule.

Firms Applying Now May Get a Refund

Crypto exchanges and wallet custodians currently register with the FCA under anti-money laundering rules. From 25 October 2027, activities including crypto custody will require authorisation under the UK’s new financial services regime.

The FCA started accepting applications under the new regime on 30 September 2026, but its proposed single fee for firms also applying for payments or e-money registration is still under consultation. Those firms must pay both fees for now.

If the rule is adopted, the FCA says it will refund the difference, saving firms up to £5,640, the highest fee tier for payment and e-money registrations. However, the actual saving will depend on the specific permissions each applicant seeks.

Overall, the regulator expects the single-fee rule to benefit up to 40 applicants, including early filers eligible for a refund.

A Separate Change to Annual Fees

The proposal also deals with what firms pay when they surrender their FCA authorisation. A firm applying to withdraw a permission currently pays the full annual fee for that year regardless of when the application is made (so if it's an April application it still pays the full annual fee).

The FCA proposes a 25% charge for applications made from April to June, with that percentage increasing each quarter to 100% for applications made from January to March.

The regulator wants to launch the new annual fee schedule on 1 April 2027. If their systems aren't ready then it would be a year later. The consultation closes 19 January 2027 and the initial crypto application window closes 28 February.

Businesses who are filing their payments and crypto applications prior to the FCA settling the fee rule will need to budget for both charges. Any refund will be subject to the final outcome of the rule.
